tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). action.description:
The action to perform:

* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

lines: # Neo4j graph tutorial
Hands-on lessons on graph databases with Neo4j — from Cypher basics to graph algorithms,
-vector search and GraphRAG — with every query's recorded output.
+vector search, GraphRAG, LangGraph agents, and a graph + vector biographical memory for an
+AI companion — with every query's recorded output.
## Quick start
```bash
-cp .env.example .env              # set NEO4J_PASSWORD; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is optional
+cp .env.example .env              # set NEO4J_PASSWORD; LLM_* for lessons 7–10
docker compose up -d --build      # Neo4j 5 + APOC + Graph Data Science
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
| 4 | [Graph algorithms and Python](lessons/04-graph-algorithms-and-python.md) | GDS projections, PageRank, Louvain, similarity, write-back, Python driver |
| 5 | [Vectors and GraphRAG](lessons/05-vectors-and-graphrag.md) | Vector indexes, local embeddings, hybrid vector + graph retrieval |
| 6 | [Graphs in AI and agents](lessons/06-graphs-in-ai-and-agents.md) | Agent memory, graph tools, when embeddings help |
+| 7 | [LangGraph agent with graph tools](lessons/07-langgraph-agent-with-graph-tools.md) | `StateGraph`, `ToolNode`, checkpointer, read-only Cypher tool |
+| 8 | [Memory design for companions](lessons/08-memory-design-for-companions.md) | Memory kinds, life graph, episodes, bi-temporal facts, boundaries |
+| 9 | [The memory write path](lessons/09-memory-write-path.md) | Structured extraction, entity resolution, dedupe, supersede, plans |
+| 10 | [Recall and the companion chat](lessons/10-companion-recall-and-chat.md) | Hybrid recall, LangGraph companion, terminal CLI, two-session demo |
+## LLM settings (lessons 7–10)
+Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling works (OpenAI, DeepInfra, OpenRouter,
+Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM...). Set in `.env`:
+| Key | |
+| `LLM_BASE_URL` | e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `http://localhost:11434/v1` |
+| `LLM_MODEL` | chat model name |
+| `LLM_API_KEY` | key (any value for local servers) |
+| `LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL` | optional, model for memory extraction (defaults to `LLM_MODEL`) |
+| `LLM_TEMPERATURE` | chat temperature |
+| `COMPANION_USER`, `COMPANION_NAME` | default user and companion names |
+Embeddings run locally (`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` via fastembed), no key needed.
## Files
| `team_graph.py` | Lesson 4 — Python driver patterns |
| `embed.py` | Lesson 5 — local embeddings + vector index |
| `graphrag.py` | Lesson 5 — GraphRAG retrieval (+ Claude answer if a key is set) |
+| `team_agent.py` | Lesson 7 — LangGraph agent with graph tools |
+| `companion/` | Lessons 8–10 — memory schema, store, extraction, LangGraph companion, CLI, demo |
+| `lessons/outputs/` | Recorded runs for lessons 7 and 10 |
## Common commands
docker compose logs -f neo4j      # logs
docker compose stop               # stop, keep data
docker compose down -v            # stop and DELETE all data
+.venv/bin/python team_agent.py    # Lesson 7 agent (interactive)
+.venv/bin/python -m companion     # Lesson 10 companion chat (/help for commands)
+.venv/bin/python -m companion.demo   # scripted two-session companion demo
.venv/bin/python graphrag.py "Who should own our new Rust performance work?"
> **Rule of thumb:** embeddings find where to start, the graph reasons from there, the LLM
> explains the result.
-## Ideas for next lessons
+## Next
-- Agent memory: record facts from conversation with `MERGE` and time-stamped edges, recall later.
-- Graph tools for an agent: `find_experts`, `who_manages`, plus a read-only Cypher tool.
-- Graph embeddings: run `gds.fastRP` and compare with Lesson 5's text similarity.

+- [Lesson 9](09-memory-write-path.md) — extracting memories from conversation into the graph.

content.text:
The rest of the tutorial is written: lessons 7–10, each with the real output from runs against your DeepInfra model (`gemma-4-31B-it`).

- **[Lesson 7](lessons/07-langgraph-agent-with-graph-tools.md)**: a LangGraph agent ([team_agent.py](team_agent.py)) that answers questions about the team graph. It has four fixed tools plus one that runs any Cypher query in read-only mode, so the database refuses writes.
- **[Lesson 8](lessons/08-memory-design-for-companions.md)**: the memory design for a companion. It covers six memory kinds (facts, preferences, events, plans, feelings, boundaries), the people and places in the user's life, and one record per conversation. It also covers why graph plus vectors does better here than vectors alone.
- **[Lesson 9](lessons/09-memory-write-path.md)**: how the model pulls memories out of a conversation and saves them. It matches people to the ones already known, skips duplicates, and replaces facts that changed. Relative dates like "next Thursday" are turned into real dates, and you can inspect the result in the Neo4j Browser.
- **[Lesson 10](lessons/10-companion-recall-and-chat.md)**: how the companion looks up memories before each reply, and the terminal chat. The scripted demo spans two sessions a week apart. In the second, the companion opens by asking how the presentation went "yesterday", and it never brings up the ex the user asked it to avoid.

The [README](README.md) now lists lessons 7–10, the `.env` settings for the model, and the run commands. Lesson 6 links forward to the new lessons. I checked that your API key appears nowhere except `.env`, which git ignores.

To try it yourself:
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m companion --debug
```

"""Lesson 10 — the companion as a LangGraph:

    START -> recall -> respond -> remember -> END

- recall:   hybrid graph + vector retrieval from Neo4j (long-term memory)
- respond:  the LLM, given the persona, the memory block and recent turns
            (short-term memory = this thread's messages, kept by the checkpointer)
- remember: log both turns to the Episode, extract memories, write them to the graph

Per-call settings travel in config["configurable"]: thread_id (= episode id), today.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt

from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, MessagesState, StateGraph

from config import COMPANION_NAME, chat_model
from companion.extract import extract_memories
from companion.store import MemoryStore, format_context

PERSONA = """\
You are {name}, a warm, thoughtful AI companion and assistant for {user}. Today is {today}.

You have a long-term memory of {user}'s life, shown below. Use it the way a good friend would:
- Weave memories in naturally. Never list them or say "according to my memory".
- Follow up on open plans when it fits, especially ones that are due or just passed.
- Respect every boundary strictly — do not raise those topics, even indirectly.
- Only rely on memories shown here. If you don't know something, ask instead of guessing.
- Be honest that you are an AI if it comes up. Be supportive, but for a crisis or medical,
  legal or financial decisions, encourage real-world help.
- Match {user}'s tone and keep replies conversational and fairly short.

=== What you remember about {user} ===
{memory}"""

RECENT_TURNS = 16  # short-term window sent to the LLM


class CompanionState(MessagesState):
    memory_context: str
    memory_log: list[str]


def _today(config: RunnableConfig) -> dt.date:
    return config["configurable"].get("today") or dt.date.today()


def build_companion(store: MemoryStore):
    llm = chat_model()

    def recall(state: CompanionState, config: RunnableConfig):
        query = state["messages"][-1].content
        found = store.recall(query, today=_today(config))
        return {"memory_context": format_context(found, _today(config))}

    def respond(state: CompanionState, config: RunnableConfig):
        today = _today(config)
        system = SystemMessage(PERSONA.format(
            name=COMPANION_NAME, user=store.user_name,
            today=f"{today.isoformat()} ({today.strftime('%A')})",
            memory=state["memory_context"],
        ))
        recent = state["messages"][-RECENT_TURNS:]
        while recent and not isinstance(recent[0], HumanMessage):  # start the window on a user turn
            recent = recent[1:]
        return {"messages": [llm.invoke([system, *recent])]}

    def remember(state: CompanionState, config: RunnableConfig):
        episode_id = config["configurable"]["thread_id"]
        user_msg = next(m for m in reversed(state["messages"]) if isinstance(m, HumanMessage)).content
        reply = state["messages"][-1].content
        store.log_turn(episode_id, store.user_name, user_msg)
        store.log_turn(episode_id, COMPANION_NAME, reply)
        extraction = extract_memories(
            store.user_name, user_msg, reply,
            candidates=store.extraction_candidates(user_msg),
            entities=store.known_entities(),
            today=_today(config),
        )
        return {"memory_log": store.apply(extraction, episode_id)}

    g = StateGraph(CompanionState)
    g.add_node("recall", recall)
    g.add_node("respond", respond)
    g.add_node("remember", remember)
    g.add_edge(START, "recall")
    g.add_edge("recall", "respond")
    g.add_edge("respond", "remember")
    g.add_edge("remember", END)
    return g.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())


def greeting(store: MemoryStore, today: dt.date) -> str:
    """Opening line for a new session, so the companion can follow up proactively."""
    found = store.recall("how are things going, plans and recent events", today=today)
    if not any(found[k] for k in ("core", "semantic", "people", "episodes")):
        return f"Hi {store.user_name}, I'm {COMPANION_NAME}. I'd love to get to know you — how's your day going?"
    system = PERSONA.format(name=COMPANION_NAME, user=store.user_name,
                            today=f"{today.isoformat()} ({today.strftime('%A')})",
                            memory=format_context(found, today))
    prompt = (f"{store.user_name} just opened a new chat. Greet them in one or two sentences. "
              "If an open plan is due or has just passed, ask how it went; otherwise pick up "
              "naturally from your last conversation.")
    return chat_model().invoke([SystemMessage(system), HumanMessage(prompt)]).content


def seed_thread(app, thread_id: str, text: str) -> None:
    """Put the greeting into the thread's short-term memory as the companion's first turn."""
    app.update_state({"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}},
                     {"messages": [AIMessage(text)]}, as_node="respond")

content.text:
**When extraction happens:** yes, there's a dedicated node, and it runs after every chat turn. The companion graph is `START → recall → respond → remember → END`, and `remember` ([graph.py:73](companion/graph.py:73)) runs on every message. It does four things, in order:

1. Logs both turns (your message and the reply) to the current conversation's record in Neo4j.
2. Finds the existing memories the new information might update: the 10 closest by vector search on your message, plus every open plan ([store.py:252](companion/store.py:252)).
3. Calls the extraction model with only the **latest exchange**, plus today's date, the known people and places, and those existing memories.
4. Writes the result to the graph: new memories, near-duplicates reinforced instead of stored again, changed facts replaced, plans marked done.

Separately, when you type `/new` or `/quit`, one more call summarizes the whole conversation and records its mood.

**Weaknesses of that design** (worth knowing before harder scenarios):

| Issue | Example |
|---|---|
| The extractor sees one exchange, not the conversation | "I asked Sam to move in." … next turn: "She said yes!" The extractor doesn't know who "she" is. |
| It blocks you | The reply prints first, but you can't type until extraction finishes. |
| An LLM call on every turn | Even "lol ok" costs an extraction call. |
| It only checks the 10 closest existing memories | A contradiction phrased very differently may not be caught, so the old fact is never replaced. |

Common alternatives:
- **Run extraction in the background**, so you never wait on it.
- **A memory tool the chat model calls itself** when it decides something is worth saving.
- **An end-of-conversation pass** that reads the whole transcript.

The usual best setup is a hybrid: a quick per-turn pass that also sees the last few turns, plus a "sleep" pass at the end of each conversation. That pass resolves "she", merges duplicates, and updates the summaries of people and places.

**More complex scenarios**, and how the current system would handle them:

| Scenario | Current handling |
|---|---|
| Corrections ("actually it was Tuesday, not Thursday") | ✅ The fact is replaced, if the old memory is among the 10 checked. |
| Questions about the past ("where did I live before Portland?") | ❌ Replaced facts are left out of recall, so it can't answer. |
| A relationship changes (partner → ex, then "don't bring them up") | ⚠️ A new boundary works, but the relationship link to that person is never updated. |
| Two people with the same name (Sam the coworker vs Sam the cousin) | ❌ Name matching would merge them into one person. |
| Recurring dates (birthdays, anniversaries) | ❌ No yearly repeat; a plan is done after it happens once. |
| "Forget everything about Jordan" | ⚠️ `/forget` deletes one memory, not a person and everything about them. |
| Multi-hop ("does anyone in my family work in healthcare?") | ⚠️ Recall only goes one step from a person, and the family relationships aren't checked. |
| Facts spread across several turns | ❌ The extractor sees only one exchange at a time. |
| Sensitive information (health, mental state) | ⚠️ It's stored like any other memory, with no separate level of care. |

Lesson 11 could turn this table into a **test suite**: scripted multi-session conversations with checks such as "the boundary never leaks", "the old address can be found via history" and "the two Sams stay separate". It would show which ones fail, then fix them with the windowed + end-of-conversation extraction, history-aware recall, recurring events and person-level forgetting.

"""What the extraction LLM returns after each exchange (validated with Pydantic)."""
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

EntityKind = Literal["person", "pet", "place", "organization", "activity", "thing"]
MemoryKind = Literal["fact", "preference", "event", "plan", "feeling", "boundary"]


class EntityOut(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Canonical name, e.g. 'Maya' or 'Portland'")
    kind: EntityKind
    aliases: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Other names used, e.g. 'my sister'")
    summary: str = Field(default="", description="One short line describing it")


class RelationOut(BaseModel):
    source: str = Field(description="'user' for the user, otherwise an entity name")
    target: str = Field(description="An entity name")
    type: str = Field(description="snake_case relation, e.g. sister, partner, works_at, lives_in, owns")
    since: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date or year if stated")


class MemoryOut(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(description="Standalone third-person statement, e.g. 'Alex's sister Maya lives in Denver'")
    kind: MemoryKind
    about: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="'user' and/or entity names it concerns")
    importance: int = Field(ge=1, le=10, description="1 trivia ... 10 core identity / major life event")
    occurred_on: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date when an event happened")
    due_on: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date a plan is due")
    supersedes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of existing memories this replaces")


class Extraction(BaseModel):
    entities: list[EntityOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    relations: list[RelationOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    memories: list[MemoryOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    invalidate: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of memories no longer true, with no replacement")
    completed_plans: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of plan memories that have now happened or been cancelled")


class EpisodeSummary(BaseModel):
    summary: str = Field(description="3-5 sentences: what was discussed and anything left open")
    mood: str = Field(description="The user's overall mood in a few words")
"""Lessons 9-10 — MemoryStore: writes memories into the graph and recalls them for a turn.

Write path (Lesson 9):  resolve entities -> link relations -> dedupe -> supersede -> store
Read path  (Lesson 10): core profile + semantic (vector) + entity hop (graph) + follow-ups
                        + recent episodes, ranked by similarity, importance and recency
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import uuid

from fastembed import TextEmbedding

from config import EMBED_MODEL
from companion.models import Extraction
from companion.schema import ensure_schema

_embedder: TextEmbedding | None = None


def embed(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    global _embedder
    _embedder = _embedder or TextEmbedding(EMBED_MODEL)
    return [v.tolist() for v in _embedder.embed(texts)]


def _new_id(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def _to_date(value: str | None) -> dt.date | None:
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:  # "2019" or "next spring" stay in the memory text instead
        return None


# Duplicate threshold on Neo4j's 0-1 rescaled cosine (0.975 ≈ raw cosine 0.95).
DUPLICATE_SCORE = 0.975
# Entity match threshold when names differ ("Mom" vs "my mother").
ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE = 0.93


class MemoryStore:
    def __init__(self, driver, user_name: str):
        self.driver = driver
        self.user_name = user_name
        self.user = f"user:{user_name.lower()}"
        ensure_schema(driver)
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (u:Entity:User {id: $user})
            ON CREATE SET u.created_at = datetime()
            SET u.name = $name, u.user = $user, u.kind = 'self'
            WITH u CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(u, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            name=user_name, vec=embed([f"{user_name}, the user"])[0],
        )

    def _q(self, query: str, **params) -> list[dict]:
        records, _, _ = self.driver.execute_query(query, user=self.user, **params)
        return [r.data() for r in records]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ episodes
    def start_episode(self, on: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
        """Open a conversation episode. `on` backdates it (used by the scripted demo)."""
        episode_id = _new_id("ep")
        self._q(
            """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (prev:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE prev.ended_at IS NOT NULL
            WITH prev ORDER BY prev.started_at DESC LIMIT 1
            CREATE (ep:Episode {id: $id, user: $user,
                                started_at: CASE WHEN $on IS NULL THEN datetime()
                                                 ELSE datetime({date: $on, hour: 12}) END})
            FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN prev IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END | MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(ep))
            """,
            id=episode_id, on=on,
        )
        return episode_id

    def log_turn(self, episode_id: str, role: str, text: str) -> None:
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            CREATE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx: COUNT { (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() },
                                             role: $role, text: $text, at: datetime()})
            """,
            ep=episode_id, role=role, text=text,
        )

    def episode_transcript(self, episode_id: str) -> str:
        rows = self._q(
            "MATCH (:Episode {id: $ep})-[:HAS_TURN]->(t) RETURN t.role AS role, t.text AS text ORDER BY t.idx",
            ep=episode_id,
        )
        return "\n".join(f"{r['role']}: {r['text']}" for r in rows)

    def end_episode(self, episode_id: str, summary: str | None, mood: str | None) -> None:
        if not summary:  # nothing was said: drop the empty episode
            self._q("MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep}) WHERE NOT (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() DETACH DELETE ep", ep=episode_id)
            return
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            SET ep.ended_at = datetime(), ep.summary = $summary, ep.mood = $mood
            WITH ep CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(ep, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            ep=episode_id, summary=summary, mood=mood, vec=embed([summary])[0],
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ entities
    def resolve_entity(self, name: str, kind: str = "thing", aliases=(), summary: str = "") -> str:
        """Find-or-create an entity: exact name/alias, then embedding similarity, then new."""
        if name.strip().lower() in {"user", "me", "i", self.user_name.lower()}:
            return self.user
        names = [n.lower() for n in [name, *aliases]]
        hit = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
            WHERE toLower(e.name) IN $names OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) IN $names)
            RETURN e.id AS id LIMIT 1
            """,
            names=names,
        )
        vec = embed([f"{name} ({kind}): {summary}"])[0]
        if not hit:
            hit = self._q(
                """
                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 5, $vec) YIELD node, score
                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.kind = $kind AND score >= $min
                RETURN node.id AS id ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 1
                """,
                vec=vec, kind=kind, min=ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE,
            )
        entity_id = hit[0]["id"] if hit else _new_id("e")
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (e:Entity {id: $id})
            ON CREATE SET e.user = $user, e.name = $name, e.kind = $kind, e.created_at = datetime()
            SET e.aliases = [a IN apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(e.aliases, []) + $aliases) WHERE toLower(a) <> toLower(e.name)],
                e.summary = CASE WHEN $summary <> '' THEN $summary ELSE e.summary END
            WITH e CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(e, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            id=entity_id, name=name, kind=kind, aliases=list(aliases), summary=summary, vec=vec,
        )
        return entity_id

    def _lookup(self, name: str, known: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
        """Map a name used in a memory/relation to an entity id without creating junk nodes."""
        key = name.strip().lower()
        if key in {"user", "me", "i", self.user_name.lower()}:
            return self.user
        if key in known:
            return known[key]
        hit = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
            WHERE toLower(e.name) = $n OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) = $n)
            RETURN e.id AS id LIMIT 1
            """,
            n=key,
        )
        return hit[0]["id"] if hit else None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write path
    def apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Store one extraction. Returns a human-readable log of what changed."""
        log: list[str] = []
        known: dict[str, str] = {}
        for ent in ex.entities:
            eid = self.resolve_entity(ent.name, ent.kind, ent.aliases, ent.summary)
            for n in [ent.name, *ent.aliases]:
                known[n.lower()] = eid

        for rel in ex.relations:
            a, b = self._lookup(rel.source, known), self._lookup(rel.target, known)
            if a and b and a != b:
                self._q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b})
                    MERGE (a)-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(b)
                    SET r.since = coalesce($since, r.since), r.updated_at = datetime()
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, type=rel.type, since=rel.since,
                )
                log.append(f"linked {rel.source} -{rel.type}-> {rel.target}")

        for mid in ex.invalidate:
            if self._q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                SET m.invalidated_at = datetime() RETURN m.text AS text
                """, id=mid,
            ):
                log.append(f"retired {mid}")
        for mid in ex.completed_plans:
            if self._q("MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user, kind: 'plan'}) SET m.status = 'done' RETURN m.id", id=mid):
                log.append(f"plan done {mid}")

        vectors = embed([m.text for m in ex.memories]) if ex.memories else []
        for mem, vec in zip(ex.memories, vectors):
            dup = self._q(
                """
                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', 5, $vec) YIELD node, score
                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.invalidated_at IS NULL AND score >= $min
                  AND NOT node.id IN $supersedes
                RETURN node.id AS id LIMIT 1
                """,
                vec=vec, min=DUPLICATE_SCORE, supersedes=mem.supersedes,
            )
            if dup:  # already known: reinforce instead of storing a near-copy
                self._q(
                    """
                    MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id})
                    SET m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1, m.last_confirmed = datetime(),
                        m.importance = CASE WHEN $imp > m.importance THEN $imp ELSE m.importance END
                    """,
                    id=dup[0]["id"], imp=mem.importance,
                )
                log.append(f"reinforced {dup[0]['id']}")
                continue

            mid = _new_id("m")
            about = [eid for n in (mem.about or ["user"]) if (eid := self._lookup(n, known))]
            retired = self._q(
                """
                CREATE (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user, text: $text, kind: $kind, importance: $imp,
                                  occurred_on: $occurred, due_on: $due,
                                  status: CASE WHEN $kind = 'plan' THEN 'open' ELSE null END,
                                  created_at: datetime(), access_count: 0})
                WITH m CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(m, 'embedding', $vec)
                WITH m
                CALL (m) { UNWIND $about AS eid MATCH (e:Entity {id: eid}) MERGE (m)-[:ABOUT]->(e) }
                CALL (m) { MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep}) MERGE (m)-[:FROM]->(ep) }
                CALL (m) {
                  UNWIND $supersedes AS old_id
                  MATCH (old:Memory {id: old_id, user: $user}) WHERE old.invalidated_at IS NULL
                  SET old.invalidated_at = datetime()
                  MERGE (m)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old)
                  RETURN collect(old.id) AS retired
                }
                RETURN retired
                """,
                id=mid, text=mem.text, kind=mem.kind, imp=mem.importance,
                occurred=_to_date(mem.occurred_on), due=_to_date(mem.due_on),
                vec=vec, about=about, ep=episode_id or "", supersedes=mem.supersedes,
            )[0]["retired"]
            log.append(f"+ [{mem.kind}] {mem.text}" + (f"  (replaces {', '.join(retired)})" if retired else ""))
        return log

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ read path
    def extraction_candidates(self, text: str, k: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
        """Existing current memories the extractor may update or retire, with their ids."""
        return self._q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', $k, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.status AS status
            UNION
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.status AS status
            """,
            k=k, vec=embed([text])[0],
        )

    def known_entities(self) -> list[str]:
        rows = self._q(
            "MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self' RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind ORDER BY e.name"
        )
        return [f"{r['name']} ({r['kind']})" for r in rows]

    def recall(self, query: str, k: int = 8, today: dt.date | None = None) -> dict:
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        vec = embed([query])[0]
        # Core profile: every boundary + the most important stable facts and preferences.
        core = self._q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'boundary'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
              RETURN m
              UNION
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                AND m.kind IN ['fact', 'preference'] AND m.importance >= 6
              WITH m ORDER BY m.importance DESC, m.created_at DESC LIMIT 8
              RETURN m
            }
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text
            ORDER BY CASE m.kind WHEN 'boundary' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, m.importance DESC
            """
        )
        # Semantic: vector similarity re-ranked by importance and recency (feelings fade fast).
        semantic = self._q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', 50, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
            WITH m, score,
                 duration.inDays(coalesce(m.last_accessed, m.created_at), datetime()).days AS age
            WITH m, score, 0.6 * score + 0.25 * m.importance / 10.0
                 + 0.15 * exp(-age / CASE m.kind WHEN 'feeling' THEN 7.0 ELSE 90.0 END) AS rank
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.occurred_on AS occurred_on,
                   round(score, 3) AS score, round(rank, 3) AS rank
            ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT $k
            """,
            vec=vec, k=k,
        )
        # Graph hop: entities named (or meant) in the message -> their memories and relations.
        entities = self._q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
                AND any(n IN [e.name] + coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE size(n) > 2 AND toLower($q) CONTAINS toLower(n))
              RETURN e
              UNION
              CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 3, $vec) YIELD node AS e, score
              WITH e, score WHERE e.user = $user AND e.kind <> 'self' AND score >= 0.85
              RETURN e
            }
            WITH e WHERE NOT EXISTS {  // entities protected by a boundary are never surfaced
              MATCH (:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) }
            OPTIONAL MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]-(e)
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
              WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
            WITH e, r, m ORDER BY m.importance DESC
            WITH e, head(collect(r.type)) AS relation, collect(m {.id, .kind, .text})[..5] AS memories
            RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary, relation, memories
            """,
            q=query, vec=vec,
        )
        people = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity)
            WHERE NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL }
            RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, r.type AS relation ORDER BY e.kind, e.name LIMIT 25
            """
        )
        followups = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.due_on IS NOT NULL
              AND m.due_on >= $today - duration({days: 14}) AND m.due_on <= $today + duration({days: 14})
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.due_on AS due_on ORDER BY m.due_on
            """,
            today=today,
        )
        episodes = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE ep.summary IS NOT NULL
            RETURN ep.started_at AS at, ep.summary AS summary, ep.mood AS mood
            ORDER BY ep.started_at DESC LIMIT 3
            """
        )
        touched = [m["id"] for m in semantic] + [m["id"] for e in entities for m in e["memories"]]
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory) WHERE m.id IN $ids
            SET m.last_accessed = datetime(), m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1
            """,
            ids=touched,
        )
        return {"core": core, "semantic": semantic, "entities": entities, "people": people,
                "followups": followups, "episodes": episodes}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ inspection
    def memories(self, kind: str | None = None, include_retired: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user})
            WHERE ($kind IS NULL OR m.kind = $kind) AND ($all OR m.invalidated_at IS NULL)
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.importance AS importance,
                   m.status AS status, m.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired,
                   m.created_at AS created_at, collect(e.name) AS about
            ORDER BY created_at
            """,
            kind=kind, all=include_retired,
        )

    def timeline(self) -> list[dict]:
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user})
            WHERE m.kind IN ['event', 'plan'] AND coalesce(m.occurred_on, m.due_on) IS NOT NULL
            RETURN coalesce(m.occurred_on, m.due_on) AS date, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text,
                   m.status AS status, m.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired
            ORDER BY date
            """
        )

    def history(self, memory_id: str) -> list[dict]:
        """A memory and every version it replaced, newest first."""
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH path = (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user})-[:SUPERSEDES*0..]->(old)
            RETURN old.id AS id, old.text AS text, old.created_at AS created_at,
                   old.invalidated_at AS retired_at ORDER BY length(path)
            """,
            id=memory_id,
        )

    def forget(self, memory_id: str) -> bool:
        """User-requested forgetting: hard delete (privacy beats provenance here)."""
        return bool(self._q(
            "MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WITH m, m.id AS id DETACH DELETE m RETURN id",
            id=memory_id,
        ))

    def wipe(self) -> None:
        """Delete everything stored for this user (used by the demo to start clean)."""
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (n) WHERE (n:Memory OR n:Entity OR n:Episode) AND n.user = $user
            OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:HAS_TURN]->(t:Turn)
            DETACH DELETE n, t
            """
        )
        self.__init__(self.driver, self.user_name)


def format_context(r: dict, today: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
    """Render a recall() result as the memory block placed in the system prompt."""
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    out: list[str] = []
    if r["core"]:
        out.append("Core profile:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {m['text']}" for m in r["core"]))
    if r["people"]:
        out.append("People and things in their life:\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {p['name']} ({p['relation']})" for p in r["people"]))
    if r["followups"]:
        out.append("Open plans to follow up on (today is " + today.isoformat() + "):\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {m['text']} (due {m['due_on']})" for m in r["followups"]))
    seen = {m["text"] for m in r["core"] + r["followups"]}
    relevant = [m for m in r["semantic"] if m["text"] not in seen]
    for e in r["entities"]:
        relevant += [m for m in e["memories"] if m["text"] not in seen | {x["text"] for x in relevant}]
    if relevant:
        out.append("Relevant memories:\n" + "\n".join(f"- [{m['kind']}] {m['text']}" for m in relevant))
    if r["episodes"]:
        out.append("Recent conversations:\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {str(e['at'])[:10]} (mood: {e['mood']}): {e['summary']}" for e in r["episodes"]))
    return "\n\n".join(out) or "(No memories yet — this is a new relationship.)"

"""What the extraction LLM returns after each exchange (validated with Pydantic)."""
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

EntityKind = Literal["person", "pet", "place", "organization", "activity", "thing"]
MemoryKind = Literal["fact", "preference", "event", "plan", "feeling", "boundary"]


class EntityOut(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Canonical name, e.g. 'Maya' or 'Portland'")
    kind: EntityKind
    aliases: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Other names used, e.g. 'my sister'")
    summary: str = Field(default="", description="One short line describing it")


class RelationOut(BaseModel):
    source: str = Field(description="'user' for the user, otherwise an entity name")
    target: str = Field(description="An entity name")
    type: str = Field(description="snake_case relation, e.g. sister, partner, works_at, lives_in, owns")
    since: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date or year if stated")


class MemoryOut(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(description="Standalone third-person statement, e.g. 'Alex's sister Maya lives in Denver'")
    kind: MemoryKind
    about: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="'user' and/or entity names it concerns")
    importance: int = Field(ge=1, le=10, description="1 trivia ... 10 core identity / major life event")
    occurred_on: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date when an event happened")
    due_on: str | None = Field(default=None, description="ISO date a plan is due")
    supersedes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of existing memories this replaces")


class Extraction(BaseModel):
    entities: list[EntityOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    relations: list[RelationOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    memories: list[MemoryOut] = Field(default_factory=list)
    invalidate: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of memories no longer true, with no replacement")
    completed_plans: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="ids of plan memories that have now happened or been cancelled")


class EpisodeSummary(BaseModel):
    summary: str = Field(description="3-5 sentences: what was discussed and anything left open")
    mood: str = Field(description="The user's overall mood in a few words")
"""Lessons 9-10 — MemoryStore: writes memories into the graph and recalls them for a turn.

Write path (Lesson 9):  resolve entities -> link relations -> dedupe -> supersede -> store
Read path  (Lesson 10): core profile + semantic (vector) + entity hop (graph) + follow-ups
                        + recent episodes, ranked by similarity, importance and recency
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import uuid

from fastembed import TextEmbedding

from config import EMBED_MODEL
from companion.models import Extraction
from companion.schema import ensure_schema

_embedder: TextEmbedding | None = None


def embed(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    global _embedder
    _embedder = _embedder or TextEmbedding(EMBED_MODEL)
    return [v.tolist() for v in _embedder.embed(texts)]


def _new_id(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def _to_date(value: str | None) -> dt.date | None:
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:  # "2019" or "next spring" stay in the memory text instead
        return None


# Duplicate threshold on Neo4j's 0-1 rescaled cosine (0.975 ≈ raw cosine 0.95).
DUPLICATE_SCORE = 0.975
# Entity match threshold when names differ ("Mom" vs "my mother").
ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE = 0.93


class MemoryStore:
    def __init__(self, driver, user_name: str):
        self.driver = driver
        self.user_name = user_name
        self.user = f"user:{user_name.lower()}"
        ensure_schema(driver)
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (u:Entity:User {id: $user})
            ON CREATE SET u.created_at = datetime()
            SET u.name = $name, u.user = $user, u.kind = 'self'
            WITH u CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(u, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            name=user_name, vec=embed([f"{user_name}, the user"])[0],
        )

    def _q(self, query: str, **params) -> list[dict]:
        records, _, _ = self.driver.execute_query(query, user=self.user, **params)
        return [r.data() for r in records]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ episodes
    def start_episode(self, on: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
        """Open a conversation episode. `on` backdates it (used by the scripted demo)."""
        episode_id = _new_id("ep")
        self._q(
            """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (prev:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE prev.ended_at IS NOT NULL
            WITH prev ORDER BY prev.started_at DESC LIMIT 1
            CREATE (ep:Episode {id: $id, user: $user,
                                started_at: CASE WHEN $on IS NULL THEN datetime()
                                                 ELSE datetime({date: $on, hour: 12}) END})
            FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN prev IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END | MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(ep))
            """,
            id=episode_id, on=on,
        )
        return episode_id

    def log_turn(self, episode_id: str, role: str, text: str) -> None:
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            CREATE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx: COUNT { (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() },
                                             role: $role, text: $text, at: datetime()})
            """,
            ep=episode_id, role=role, text=text,
        )

    def episode_transcript(self, episode_id: str) -> str:
        rows = self._q(
            "MATCH (:Episode {id: $ep})-[:HAS_TURN]->(t) RETURN t.role AS role, t.text AS text ORDER BY t.idx",
            ep=episode_id,
        )
        return "\n".join(f"{r['role']}: {r['text']}" for r in rows)

    def end_episode(self, episode_id: str, summary: str | None, mood: str | None) -> None:
        if not summary:  # nothing was said: drop the empty episode
            self._q("MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep}) WHERE NOT (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() DETACH DELETE ep", ep=episode_id)
            return
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            SET ep.ended_at = datetime(), ep.summary = $summary, ep.mood = $mood
            WITH ep CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(ep, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            ep=episode_id, summary=summary, mood=mood, vec=embed([summary])[0],
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ entities
    def resolve_entity(self, name: str, kind: str = "thing", aliases=(), summary: str = "") -> str:
        """Find-or-create an entity: exact name/alias, then embedding similarity, then new."""
        if name.strip().lower() in {"user", "me", "i", self.user_name.lower()}:
            return self.user
        names = [n.lower() for n in [name, *aliases]]
        hit = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
            WHERE toLower(e.name) IN $names OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) IN $names)
            RETURN e.id AS id LIMIT 1
            """,
            names=names,
        )
        vec = embed([f"{name} ({kind}): {summary}"])[0]
        if not hit:
            hit = self._q(
                """
                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 5, $vec) YIELD node, score
                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.kind = $kind AND score >= $min
                RETURN node.id AS id ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 1
                """,
                vec=vec, kind=kind, min=ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE,
            )
        entity_id = hit[0]["id"] if hit else _new_id("e")
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (e:Entity {id: $id})
            ON CREATE SET e.user = $user, e.name = $name, e.kind = $kind, e.created_at = datetime()
            SET e.aliases = [a IN apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(e.aliases, []) + $aliases) WHERE toLower(a) <> toLower(e.name)],
                e.summary = CASE WHEN $summary <> '' THEN $summary ELSE e.summary END
            WITH e CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(e, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            id=entity_id, name=name, kind=kind, aliases=list(aliases), summary=summary, vec=vec,
        )
        return entity_id

    def _lookup(self, name: str, known: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
        """Map a name used in a memory/relation to an entity id without creating junk nodes."""
        key = name.strip().lower()
        if key in {"user", "me", "i", self.user_name.lower()}:
            return self.user
        if key in known:
            return known[key]
        hit = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
            WHERE toLower(e.name) = $n OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) = $n)
            RETURN e.id AS id LIMIT 1
            """,
            n=key,
        )
        return hit[0]["id"] if hit else None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write path
    def apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Store one extraction. Returns a human-readable log of what changed."""
        log: list[str] = []
        known: dict[str, str] = {}
        for ent in ex.entities:
            eid = self.resolve_entity(ent.name, ent.kind, ent.aliases, ent.summary)
            for n in [ent.name, *ent.aliases]:
                known[n.lower()] = eid

        for rel in ex.relations:
            a, b = self._lookup(rel.source, known), self._lookup(rel.target, known)
            if a and b and a != b:
                self._q(
                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a}), (b:Entity {id: $b})
                    MERGE (a)-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(b)
                    SET r.since = coalesce($since, r.since), r.updated_at = datetime()
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, type=rel.type, since=rel.since,
                )
                log.append(f"linked {rel.source} -{rel.type}-> {rel.target}")

        for mid in ex.invalidate:
            if self._q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                SET m.invalidated_at = datetime() RETURN m.text AS text
                """, id=mid,
            ):
                log.append(f"retired {mid}")
        for mid in ex.completed_plans:
            if self._q("MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user, kind: 'plan'}) SET m.status = 'done' RETURN m.id", id=mid):
                log.append(f"plan done {mid}")

        vectors = embed([m.text for m in ex.memories]) if ex.memories else []
        for mem, vec in zip(ex.memories, vectors):
            dup = self._q(
                """
                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', 5, $vec) YIELD node, score
                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.invalidated_at IS NULL AND score >= $min
                  AND NOT node.id IN $supersedes
                RETURN node.id AS id LIMIT 1
                """,
                vec=vec, min=DUPLICATE_SCORE, supersedes=mem.supersedes,
            )
            if dup:  # already known: reinforce instead of storing a near-copy
                self._q(
                    """
                    MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id})
                    SET m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1, m.last_confirmed = datetime(),
                        m.importance = CASE WHEN $imp > m.importance THEN $imp ELSE m.importance END
                    """,
                    id=dup[0]["id"], imp=mem.importance,
                )
                log.append(f"reinforced {dup[0]['id']}")
                continue

            mid = _new_id("m")
            about = [eid for n in (mem.about or ["user"]) if (eid := self._lookup(n, known))]
            retired = self._q(
                """
                CREATE (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user, text: $text, kind: $kind, importance: $imp,
                                  occurred_on: $occurred, due_on: $due,
                                  status: CASE WHEN $kind = 'plan' THEN 'open' ELSE null END,
                                  created_at: datetime(), access_count: 0})
                WITH m CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(m, 'embedding', $vec)
                WITH m
                CALL (m) { UNWIND $about AS eid MATCH (e:Entity {id: eid}) MERGE (m)-[:ABOUT]->(e) }
                CALL (m) { MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep}) MERGE (m)-[:FROM]->(ep) }
                CALL (m) {
                  UNWIND $supersedes AS old_id
                  MATCH (old:Memory {id: old_id, user: $user}) WHERE old.invalidated_at IS NULL
                  SET old.invalidated_at = datetime()
                  MERGE (m)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old)
                  RETURN collect(old.id) AS retired
                }
                RETURN retired
                """,
                id=mid, text=mem.text, kind=mem.kind, imp=mem.importance,
                occurred=_to_date(mem.occurred_on), due=_to_date(mem.due_on),
                vec=vec, about=about, ep=episode_id or "", supersedes=mem.supersedes,
            )[0]["retired"]
            log.append(f"+ [{mem.kind}] {mem.text}" + (f"  (replaces {', '.join(retired)})" if retired else ""))
        return log

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ read path
    def extraction_candidates(self, text: str, k: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
        """Existing current memories the extractor may update or retire, with their ids."""
        return self._q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', $k, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.status AS status
            UNION
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.status AS status
            """,
            k=k, vec=embed([text])[0],
        )

    def known_entities(self) -> list[str]:
        rows = self._q(
            "MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self' RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind ORDER BY e.name"
        )
        return [f"{r['name']} ({r['kind']})" for r in rows]

    def recall(self, query: str, k: int = 8, today: dt.date | None = None) -> dict:
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        vec = embed([query])[0]
        # Core profile: every boundary + the most important stable facts and preferences.
        core = self._q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'boundary'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
              RETURN m
              UNION
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                AND m.kind IN ['fact', 'preference'] AND m.importance >= 6
              WITH m ORDER BY m.importance DESC, m.created_at DESC LIMIT 8
              RETURN m
            }
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text
            ORDER BY CASE m.kind WHEN 'boundary' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, m.importance DESC
            """
        )
        # Semantic: vector similarity re-ranked by importance and recency (feelings fade fast).
        semantic = self._q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('memory_vec', 50, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
            WITH m, score,
                 duration.inDays(coalesce(m.last_accessed, m.created_at), datetime()).days AS age
            WITH m, score, 0.6 * score + 0.25 * m.importance / 10.0
                 + 0.15 * exp(-age / CASE m.kind WHEN 'feeling' THEN 7.0 ELSE 90.0 END) AS rank
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.occurred_on AS occurred_on,
                   round(score, 3) AS score, round(rank, 3) AS rank
            ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT $k
            """,
            vec=vec, k=k,
        )
        # Graph hop: entities named (or meant) in the message -> their memories and relations.
        entities = self._q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
                AND any(n IN [e.name] + coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE size(n) > 2 AND toLower($q) CONTAINS toLower(n))
              RETURN e
              UNION
              CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 3, $vec) YIELD node AS e, score
              WITH e, score WHERE e.user = $user AND e.kind <> 'self' AND score >= 0.85
              RETURN e
            }
            WITH e WHERE NOT EXISTS {  // entities protected by a boundary are never surfaced
              MATCH (:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) }
            OPTIONAL MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]-(e)
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
              WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
            WITH e, r, m ORDER BY m.importance DESC
            WITH e, head(collect(r.type)) AS relation, collect(m {.id, .kind, .text})[..5] AS memories
            RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary, relation, memories
            """,
            q=query, vec=vec,
        )
        people = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity)
            WHERE NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL }
            RETURN e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, r.type AS relation ORDER BY e.kind, e.name LIMIT 25
            """
        )
        followups = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.due_on IS NOT NULL
              AND m.due_on >= $today - duration({days: 14}) AND m.due_on <= $today + duration({days: 14})
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.due_on AS due_on ORDER BY m.due_on
            """,
            today=today,
        )
        episodes = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE ep.summary IS NOT NULL
            RETURN ep.started_at AS at, ep.summary AS summary, ep.mood AS mood
            ORDER BY ep.started_at DESC LIMIT 3
            """
        )
        touched = [m["id"] for m in semantic] + [m["id"] for e in entities for m in e["memories"]]
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory) WHERE m.id IN $ids
            SET m.last_accessed = datetime(), m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1
            """,
            ids=touched,
        )
        return {"core": core, "semantic": semantic, "entities": entities, "people": people,
                "followups": followups, "episodes": episodes}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ inspection
    def memories(self, kind: str | None = None, include_retired: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user})
            WHERE ($kind IS NULL OR m.kind = $kind) AND ($all OR m.invalidated_at IS NULL)
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.importance AS importance,
                   m.status AS status, m.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired,
                   m.created_at AS created_at, collect(e.name) AS about
            ORDER BY created_at
            """,
            kind=kind, all=include_retired,
        )

    def timeline(self) -> list[dict]:
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user})
            WHERE m.kind IN ['event', 'plan'] AND coalesce(m.occurred_on, m.due_on) IS NOT NULL
            RETURN coalesce(m.occurred_on, m.due_on) AS date, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text,
                   m.status AS status, m.invalidated_at IS NOT NULL AS retired
            ORDER BY date
            """
        )

    def history(self, memory_id: str) -> list[dict]:
        """A memory and every version it replaced, newest first."""
        return self._q(
            """
            MATCH path = (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user})-[:SUPERSEDES*0..]->(old)
            RETURN old.id AS id, old.text AS text, old.created_at AS created_at,
                   old.invalidated_at AS retired_at ORDER BY length(path)
            """,
            id=memory_id,
        )

    def forget(self, memory_id: str) -> bool:
        """User-requested forgetting: hard delete (privacy beats provenance here)."""
        return bool(self._q(
            "MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WITH m, m.id AS id DETACH DELETE m RETURN id",
            id=memory_id,
        ))

    def wipe(self) -> None:
        """Delete everything stored for this user (used by the demo to start clean)."""
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (n) WHERE (n:Memory OR n:Entity OR n:Episode) AND n.user = $user
            OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:HAS_TURN]->(t:Turn)
            DETACH DELETE n, t
            """
        )
        self.__init__(self.driver, self.user_name)


def format_context(r: dict, today: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
    """Render a recall() result as the memory block placed in the system prompt."""
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    out: list[str] = []
    if r["core"]:
        out.append("Core profile:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {m['text']}" for m in r["core"]))
    if r["people"]:
        out.append("People and things in their life:\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {p['name']} ({p['relation']})" for p in r["people"]))
    if r["followups"]:
        out.append("Open plans to follow up on (today is " + today.isoformat() + "):\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {m['text']} (due {m['due_on']})" for m in r["followups"]))
    seen = {m["text"] for m in r["core"] + r["followups"]}
    relevant = [m for m in r["semantic"] if m["text"] not in seen]
    for e in r["entities"]:
        relevant += [m for m in e["memories"] if m["text"] not in seen | {x["text"] for x in relevant}]
    if relevant:
        out.append("Relevant memories:\n" + "\n".join(f"- [{m['kind']}] {m['text']}" for m in relevant))
    if r["episodes"]:
        out.append("Recent conversations:\n" + "\n".join(
            f"- {str(e['at'])[:10]} (mood: {e['mood']}): {e['summary']}" for e in r["episodes"]))
    return "\n\n".join(out) or "(No memories yet — this is a new relationship.)"
