questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

    # Clean up the toy example from 5.1.

    driver.execute_query("DROP INDEX toy_vec IF EXISTS")

    # One query per label, so each MATCH can use the label's name index (Lesson 3) instead

    for label in sorted({r["label"] for r in rows}):

            MATCH (n:{label} {{name: row.name}})
            SET n:Embedded, n.description = row.text
            WITH n, row
            CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(n, 'embedding', row.embedding)
            """,
            rows=[r for r in rows if r["label"] == label],
        )
    print(f"Embedded {len(rows)} nodes ({len(rows[0]['embedding'])} dims)")

        FOR (n:Embedded) ON (n.embedding)
        OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 384, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}
        """
    )
    driver.execute_query("CALL db.awaitIndexes(60)")
    print("Vector index 'embedded_vec' is online")

Lesson 13 and the recommended fixes are finished. The fast suite passes (127 tests), and every scenario except one passed on the full run. That one passed after I fixed its input.

**Scenarios:** the full run of all 13 scored 48/49. The one failure was "three gym visits became one lasting habit", and the cause was the scenario's input, not the code:
- The third gym message, "just got back from the gym, my legs are dead", was stored as a feeling: "Riley's legs feel exhausted after a workout". That's a reasonable reading.
- That memory doesn't contain "gym" and is only 0.73 similar to the two gym statuses. The clustering threshold is 0.82, so there were only two gym memories, not the three a pattern needs.
- Lowering the threshold would let unrelated memories chain together, so I added a clearer visit on 2026-11-21 instead ("Off to the gym again after work, then dinner").
- Rerunning just that scenario: 4/4. The upkeep step logged "pattern from 3 memories: Riley goes to the gym regularly" and pruned one faded memory.

I added the rerun to the end of `lessons/outputs/13-scenarios.txt` rather than replacing the original run. I didn't rerun all 13 scenarios after that change.

**Also done this turn:**
- **Ranking text:** Lesson 10 and diagram 9 in `docs/architecture.md` still showed the old ranking formula. Both now describe Lesson 13's version: 0.6 × similarity + 0.4 × strength, where strength fades with age, and memories that have faded too far are left out. Lesson 10 also no longer claims that being recalled keeps a memory fresh; only the user saying it again resets the fade.
- **`embed.py`:** it had no `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard, so importing it reran the whole embedding script. That happened once during my check; it's harmless because rerunning it gives the same result, but it's now wrapped in `main()`. `python embed.py` still works.
- **Lesson 13 results section:** it now has the results table, the story of the gym failure and the lesson from it: when a scenario fails, first check whether the input really contains what the check expects.

Nothing is committed yet. Say the word and I'll commit and push. `.env` stays out of it.

Nothing you asked for is still open; it's all committed and pushed. A few loose ends and possible next steps:

**Small loose ends**
- **Full scenario run:** after I added the extra gym visit, I only reran the `situational` scenario (4/4), not all 13. The full run before that was 48/49. A full rerun takes a while and calls the LLM, so it costs a little.
- **Out-of-date "Where to go next" in Lesson 10:** two of its suggestions are already built. The "consolidation job" is Lesson 13, and "scripted conversations as evals" is Lesson 11. They should be removed or point to those lessons.
- **Your `.env`:** it still has the unused `ANTHROPIC_*` lines. You can delete them; I didn't touch the file.

**Known limitations, documented but not fixed**
- `apply()` isn't atomic: if something fails halfway through, part of an extraction can be saved. Lesson 9 points this out, and a fix would wrap each write in one transaction.
- Extraction runs inline, so the user waits on it after each message. Lesson 10 suggests moving it to a background task.

**Ideas for a Lesson 14 or later**
- Graph embeddings (`gds.fastRP`) over the life graph to find related people and themes.
- Several personas or agents sharing one user's memory, each with its own view, using an `agent` property next to `user`.
- A small web UI over the terminal companion, or a dashboard of memory strength and decay over time.

I'd do the first two loose ends next: fix Lesson 10's list, then rerun all 13 scenarios to confirm 49/49. Want me to?

content.content:
become one piece of general knowledge.

**Clustering uses complete linkage.** A memory joins a cluster only if it's similar to
*every* member, not just one. I measured the threshold rather than guessing it:

```
                                   gym   gym after work   leg day   rock climbing   pizza
Riley is at the gym               1.00        0.91          0.89        0.81         0.69
Riley went to the gym after work  0.91        1.00          0.84        0.82         0.72
Riley is heading to the gym...    0.89        0.84          1.00        0.78         0.65
```

At 0.82, the gym sentences cluster. Rock climbing would chain in through "gym after work"
(0.82) under single linkage, but complete linkage keeps it out (0.78 to "leg day"). The pattern
writer can still decline a cluster that isn't a habit (airport, dentist, post office).

## What the tests and evals found

`consolidate()` takes the pattern writer as an argument (`writer=find_pattern` in
production, a lambda in tests). **Passing the LLM in** is what lets the clustering, linking
and pruning be tested exactly and for free, while the LLM part gets its own eval.

### Results

Full run: [outputs/13-scenarios.txt](outputs/13-scenarios.txt).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Fast tests (`pytest -q`, no LLM) | 127 passed |
| Lesson 13 LLM evals, 3 runs each | 6/6 |
| Extraction evals (Lesson 11), `EVAL_TRIALS=3` | 10/10 |
| Scenarios, all 13 | 48/49 on the first run; 49/49 after the fix below |

The one failure was the habit check, and it was the **scenario's** fault, not the code's. The
third gym visit was "just got back from the gym, my legs are dead", which the extractor
(reasonably) stored as a *feeling*: "Riley's legs feel exhausted after a workout". No "gym",
and only 0.73 similar to the gym statuses, so there were just two gym memories and no cluster
of three. Lowering the threshold would have "fixed" it and let unrelated memories chain
together. Instead, the scenario got a clearer extra visit, and the rerun produced:

```
✎ (upkeep) pattern from 3 memories: + [fact] Riley goes to the gym regularly.
✎ (upkeep) pruned 1 dormant status/feeling memories
```

When a scenario fails, first ask whether the *input* really contained what the check expects.

content.text:
All 13 scenarios now pass (49/49), but only after I fixed a real bug that the rerun turned up.

**The bug:** the habit check failed again, this time with four gym statuses stored. The cause was in `_clusters()` in `companion/store.py`. It went through memories in time order and put each one into the first group it fit, so an early pair could lock the rest out:
- "heading to the gym" and "just got back" paired up first (0.86 similar).
- "after work" and "before work" were each a little too far from "just got back" (0.80 and 0.81), so they formed a second pair.
- That left two pairs and no group of three, even though heading, after work and before work are all 0.85 or more similar to each other.

**The fix:** `_clusters()` now finds the largest group whose members are all similar to each other, removes it, and repeats.
- A new regression test uses these exact five sentences.
- A second new test checks that unrelated memories still can't chain together through a shared neighbour.
- In the full run, "Riley goes to the gym regularly" was the only pattern formed in any scenario, so the change didn't create false habits elsewhere.

**Also done:**
- Lesson 10's "Where to go next" points to Lessons 11–13 for what's already built and lists only what's still open.
- Lesson 13 explains how the groups are found, and its results section tells both failures: first the input didn't contain three visits, then the clustering lost a group that was there.
- The glossary's "complete linkage" entry is updated.
- Fast suite: 129 passed.

content.text:
The tutorial is in a good place: 14 lessons, every test passing, and everything pushed. What's left is optional.

**Reliability fixes**
1. **Save each memory update in one transaction.** Right now `apply()` writes several changes one after another. If one fails partway, some are saved and others aren't, for example a new fact saved but the old one it replaces never ended. Lesson 9 points out this gap.
2. **Extract memories in the background.** Today the user waits for memory extraction after every message. A background queue would make replies faster, and it brings a real lesson about concurrency: two extractions running at once could save the same memory twice.

**New lesson ideas**
3. **Graph embeddings on the life graph** (`gds.fastRP`): find related people and themes ("these three friends are all from your climbing gym"). It's a natural follow-on to Lessons 4 and 5.
4. **Several personas sharing one user's memory**, each with its own view, using an `agent` property next to `user`.
5. **A small web UI or dashboard**: the chat, plus a view of the life graph and of memory strength fading over time.

**Housekeeping**
- Delete the unused `ANTHROPIC_*` lines from your `.env`. That's a quick edit for you; I won't open the file.

My pick is 1 and 2 together as "Lesson 14: making the companion production-ready". That fixes the one known correctness gap in the code, and transactions and concurrency are worth knowing for any app built on Neo4j. Which would you like to do?

100	# the summaries dominate the embedding. Mom/mother 0.87, NYC/New York 0.93; Seattle/Boston 0.64.
101	NAME_MATCH_MIN = 0.80
102	# Sensitive memories (health, finances...) are recalled only when the message is clearly about
103	# them: (near) the best vector match for this message, not just above a fixed score. Small
104	# embedding models squeeze all scores into a narrow band (~0.63-0.80 here), so relative wins.
105	SENSITIVE_MARGIN = 0.01
106	SENSITIVE_FLOOR = 0.72
107	
108	# A memory about someone a boundary protects ("don't bring up Dana") is never recalled.
109	# The user node is excluded: a topic boundary ("don't ask about my job") is ABOUT the user,
110	# and must not hide everything else about them (found by tests/test_10_recall.py).
111	NOT_PROTECTED = """NOT EXISTS {
112	    MATCH (m)-[:ABOUT]->(protected:Entity)<-[:ABOUT]-(b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})
113	    WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) AND b <> m AND NOT protected:User }"""
114	# (Its variable names must not clash with the query it's pasted into: an outer `e` would
115	# silently turn "any entity" into "this entity" inside the EXISTS.)
116	
117	def _annual(md: str | None) -> str | None:
118	    return md if md and re.fullmatch(r"\d{2}-\d{2}", md) else None
119	
120	
121	def _next_occurrence(md: str, today: dt.date) -> dt.date | None:
122	    """Next date (from 3 days ago onward) on which a yearly 'MM-DD' falls."""
123	    month, day = map(int, md.split("-"))
124	    for year in (today.year - 1, today.year, today.year + 1):
125	        try:
126	            d = dt.date(year, month, day)
127	        except ValueError:  # Feb 29 in a non-leap year
128	            d = dt.date(year, month, 28)
129	        if d >= today - dt.timedelta(days=3):
130	            return d
131	    return None
132	
133	
134	class MemoryStore:
135	    def __init__(self, driver, user_name: str):
136	        self.driver = driver
137	        self.user_name = user_name
138	        self.user = f"user:{user_name.lower()}"
139	        ensure_schema(driver)
140	        global _ontology_loaded
141	        if not _ontology_loaded:
142	            ontology.ensure_ontology(driver)
143	            _ontology_loaded = True
144	        self._q(
145	            """
146	            MERGE (u:Entity:User {id: $user})
147	            ON CREATE SET u.created_at = datetime()
148	            SET u.name = $name, u.user = $user, u.kind = 'self'
149	            WITH u CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(u, 'embedding', $vec)
150	            """,
151	            name=user_name, vec=embed([f"{user_name}, the user"])[0],
152	        )
153	
154	    def _q(self, query: str, now: dt.datetime | None = None, **params) -> list[dict]:
155	        """Run a query with $user and $now always set ($now: the conversation's clock)."""
156	        records, _, _ = self.driver.execute_query(
157	            query, user=self.user, now=now or clock.now_for(dt.date.today()), **params)
158	        return [r.data() for r in records]
159	
160	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ episodes
161	    def start_episode(self, on: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
162	        """Open a conversation episode. `on` backdates it (used by the scripted demo)."""
163	        episode_id = _new_id("ep")
164	        self._q(
165	            """
166	            OPTIONAL MATCH (prev:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE prev.ended_at IS NOT NULL
167	            WITH prev ORDER BY prev.started_at DESC LIMIT 1
168	            CREATE (ep:Episode {id: $id, user: $user,
169	                                started_at: CASE WHEN $on IS NULL THEN datetime()
170	                                                 ELSE datetime({date: $on, hour: 12}) END})
171	            FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN prev IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END | MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(ep))
172	            """,
173	            id=episode_id, on=on,
174	        )
175	        return episode_id
176	
177	    def log_turn(self, episode_id: str, role: str, text: str) -> None:
178	        self._q(
179	            """
180	            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
181	            CREATE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx: COUNT { (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() },
182	                                             role: $role, text: $text, at: datetime()})
183	            """,
184	            ep=episode_id, role=role, text=text,
185	        )
186	
187	    def episode_turns(self, episode_id: str) -> list[dict]:
188	        return self._q(
189	            "MATCH (:Episode {id: $ep})-[:HAS_TURN]->(t) RETURN t.role AS role, t.text AS text ORDER BY t.idx",

191	        )

193	    def episode_transcript(self, episode_id: str) -> str:
194	        return "\n".join(f"{r['role']}: {r['text']}" for r in self.episode_turns(episode_id))
195	
196	    def end_episode(self, episode_id: str, summary: str | None, mood: str | None) -> None:
197	        if not summary:  # drop an empty episode; close one whose summary failed, so NEXT links it
198	            self._q(
199	                """
200	                MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
201	                CALL (ep) { WITH ep WHERE NOT (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() DETACH DELETE ep }
202	                CALL (ep) { WITH ep WHERE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() SET ep.ended_at = datetime() }
203	                """,
204	                ep=episode_id,
205	            )
206	            return
207	        self._q(
208	            """
209	            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
210	            SET ep.ended_at = datetime(), ep.summary = $summary, ep.mood = $mood
211	            WITH ep CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(ep, 'embedding', $vec)
212	            """,
213	            ep=episode_id, summary=summary, mood=mood, vec=embed([summary])[0],
214	        )

217	    def _is_user(self, name: str) -> bool:
218	        return name.strip().lower() in {"user", "me", "i", self.user, self.user_name.lower()}
219	
220	    def resolve_entity(self, name: str, kind: str = "thing", aliases=(), summary: str = "",
221	                       ref: str | None = None, new: bool = False) -> str:
222	        """Find-or-create an entity.
223	
224	        1. `ref` — the extractor pointed at a known entity id
225	        2. `new` — the extractor says it's a different entity with a known name (a second Sam)
226	        3. exact name/alias; if several share the name, the one whose summary is most similar
227	        4. embedding similarity (same kind) above ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE
228	        5. otherwise create it
229	        """
230	        if self._is_user(name):
231	            return self.user
232	        vec = embed([f"{name} ({kind}): {summary}"])[0]
233	        hit = self._q("MATCH (e:Entity {id: $id, user: $user}) RETURN e.id AS id", id=ref) if ref else []
234	        if not hit and not new:
235	            names = [n.lower() for n in [name, *aliases]]
236	            hit = self._q(
237	                """
238	                MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
239	                  AND (toLower(e.name) IN $names OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) IN $names))
240	                RETURN e.id AS id ORDER BY vector.similarity.cosine(e.embedding, $vec) DESC LIMIT 1
241	                """,
242	                names=names, vec=vec,
243	            )
244	        if not hit and not new:
245	            candidates = self._q(
246	                """
247	                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 50, $vec) YIELD node, score
248	                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.kind = $kind AND score >= $min
249	                RETURN node.id AS id, [node.name] + coalesce(node.aliases, []) AS names ORDER BY score DESC
250	                """,
251	                vec=vec, kind=kind, min=ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE,
252	            )
253	            hit = [c for c in candidates if _name_similarity([name, *aliases], c["names"]) >= NAME_MATCH_MIN][:1]
254	        entity_id = hit[0]["id"] if hit else _new_id("e")
255	        self._q(
256	            """
257	            MERGE (e:Entity {id: $id})
258	            ON CREATE SET e.user = $user, e.name = $name, e.kind = $kind, e.created_at = datetime()
259	            SET e.updated_at = datetime(), e.aliases = [a IN apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(e.aliases, []) + $aliases) WHERE toLower(a) <> toLower(e.name)],
260	                e.summary = CASE WHEN $summary <> '' THEN $summary ELSE e.summary END
261	            WITH e CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(e, 'embedding', $vec)
262	            """,
263	            id=entity_id, name=name, kind=kind, aliases=list(aliases), summary=summary, vec=vec,
264	        )
265	        return entity_id
266	
267	    def _lookup(self, name: str, known: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
268	        """Map a name or id used in a memory/relation to an entity id without creating junk nodes.
269	
270	        Names resolved in this same extraction win; otherwise an id, then the most recently
271	        updated entity with that name or alias."""
272	        key = name.strip().lower()
273	        if self._is_user(key):
274	            return self.user
275	        if key in known:
276	            return known[key]
277	        hit = self._q(
278	            """
279	            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
280	            WHERE e.id = $n OR toLower(e.name) = $n OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) = $n)
281	            RETURN e.id AS id ORDER BY CASE WHEN e.id = $n THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, e.updated_at DESC LIMIT 1
282	            """,

284	        )
285	        return hit[0]["id"] if hit else None

287	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write path
288	    def apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None = None, today: dt.date | None = None) -> list[str]:
289	        """Store one extraction. Returns a human-readable log of what changed."""
290	        today = today or dt.date.today()
291	        now = clock.now_for(today)
292	        q = partial(self._q, now=now)
293	        log: list[str] = []
294	        known: dict[str, str] = {}
295	        self.forgotten_terms: list[str] = []  # names forgotten by this call (the graph redacts its thread)

305	        # Relations go through the ontology: normalize the type, check its range, then apply

# the summaries dominate the embedding. Mom/mother 0.87, NYC/New York 0.93; Seattle/Boston 0.64.
NAME_MATCH_MIN = 0.80
# Sensitive memories (health, finances...) are recalled only when the message is clearly about
# them: (near) the best vector match for this message, not just above a fixed score. Small
# embedding models squeeze all scores into a narrow band (~0.63-0.80 here), so relative wins.
SENSITIVE_MARGIN = 0.01
SENSITIVE_FLOOR = 0.72

# A memory about someone a boundary protects ("don't bring up Dana") is never recalled.
# The user node is excluded: a topic boundary ("don't ask about my job") is ABOUT the user,
# and must not hide everything else about them (found by tests/test_10_recall.py).
NOT_PROTECTED = """NOT EXISTS {
    MATCH (m)-[:ABOUT]->(protected:Entity)<-[:ABOUT]-(b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})
    WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) AND b <> m AND NOT protected:User }"""
# (Its variable names must not clash with the query it's pasted into: an outer `e` would
# silently turn "any entity" into "this entity" inside the EXISTS.)

def _annual(md: str | None) -> str | None:
    return md if md and re.fullmatch(r"\d{2}-\d{2}", md) else None


def _next_occurrence(md: str, today: dt.date) -> dt.date | None:
    """Next date (from 3 days ago onward) on which a yearly 'MM-DD' falls."""
    month, day = map(int, md.split("-"))
    for year in (today.year - 1, today.year, today.year + 1):
        try:
            d = dt.date(year, month, day)
        except ValueError:  # Feb 29 in a non-leap year
            d = dt.date(year, month, 28)
        if d >= today - dt.timedelta(days=3):
            return d
    return None


class MemoryStore:
    def __init__(self, driver, user_name: str):
        self.driver = driver
        self.user_name = user_name
        self.user = f"user:{user_name.lower()}"
        ensure_schema(driver)
        global _ontology_loaded
        if not _ontology_loaded:
            ontology.ensure_ontology(driver)
            _ontology_loaded = True
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (u:Entity:User {id: $user})
            ON CREATE SET u.created_at = datetime()
            SET u.name = $name, u.user = $user, u.kind = 'self'
            WITH u CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(u, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            name=user_name, vec=embed([f"{user_name}, the user"])[0],
        )

    def _q(self, query: str, now: dt.datetime | None = None, **params) -> list[dict]:
        """Run a query with $user and $now always set ($now: the conversation's clock)."""
        records, _, _ = self.driver.execute_query(
            query, user=self.user, now=now or clock.now_for(dt.date.today()), **params)
        return [r.data() for r in records]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ episodes
    def start_episode(self, on: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
        """Open a conversation episode. `on` backdates it (used by the scripted demo)."""
        episode_id = _new_id("ep")
        self._q(
            """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (prev:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE prev.ended_at IS NOT NULL
            WITH prev ORDER BY prev.started_at DESC LIMIT 1
            CREATE (ep:Episode {id: $id, user: $user,
                                started_at: CASE WHEN $on IS NULL THEN datetime()
                                                 ELSE datetime({date: $on, hour: 12}) END})
            FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN prev IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END | MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(ep))
            """,
            id=episode_id, on=on,
        )
        return episode_id

    def log_turn(self, episode_id: str, role: str, text: str) -> None:
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            CREATE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx: COUNT { (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() },
                                             role: $role, text: $text, at: datetime()})
            """,
            ep=episode_id, role=role, text=text,
        )

    def episode_turns(self, episode_id: str) -> list[dict]:
        return self._q(
            "MATCH (:Episode {id: $ep})-[:HAS_TURN]->(t) RETURN t.role AS role, t.text AS text ORDER BY t.idx",
            ep=episode_id,
        )

    def episode_transcript(self, episode_id: str) -> str:
        return "\n".join(f"{r['role']}: {r['text']}" for r in self.episode_turns(episode_id))

    def end_episode(self, episode_id: str, summary: str | None, mood: str | None) -> None:
        if not summary:  # drop an empty episode; close one whose summary failed, so NEXT links it
            self._q(
                """
                MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
                CALL (ep) { WITH ep WHERE NOT (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() DETACH DELETE ep }
                CALL (ep) { WITH ep WHERE (ep)-[:HAS_TURN]->() SET ep.ended_at = datetime() }
                """,
                ep=episode_id,
            )
            return
        self._q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {id: $ep})
            SET ep.ended_at = datetime(), ep.summary = $summary, ep.mood = $mood
            WITH ep CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(ep, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            ep=episode_id, summary=summary, mood=mood, vec=embed([summary])[0],
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ entities
    def _is_user(self, name: str) -> bool:
        return name.strip().lower() in {"user", "me", "i", self.user, self.user_name.lower()}

    def resolve_entity(self, name: str, kind: str = "thing", aliases=(), summary: str = "",
                       ref: str | None = None, new: bool = False) -> str:
        """Find-or-create an entity.

        1. `ref` — the extractor pointed at a known entity id
        2. `new` — the extractor says it's a different entity with a known name (a second Sam)
        3. exact name/alias; if several share the name, the one whose summary is most similar
        4. embedding similarity (same kind) above ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE
        5. otherwise create it
        """
        if self._is_user(name):
            return self.user
        vec = embed([f"{name} ({kind}): {summary}"])[0]
        hit = self._q("MATCH (e:Entity {id: $id, user: $user}) RETURN e.id AS id", id=ref) if ref else []
        if not hit and not new:
            names = [n.lower() for n in [name, *aliases]]
            hit = self._q(
                """
                MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
                  AND (toLower(e.name) IN $names OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) IN $names))
                RETURN e.id AS id ORDER BY vector.similarity.cosine(e.embedding, $vec) DESC LIMIT 1
                """,
                names=names, vec=vec,
            )
        if not hit and not new:
            candidates = self._q(
                """
                CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('entity_vec', 50, $vec) YIELD node, score
                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.kind = $kind AND score >= $min
                RETURN node.id AS id, [node.name] + coalesce(node.aliases, []) AS names ORDER BY score DESC
                """,
                vec=vec, kind=kind, min=ENTITY_MATCH_SCORE,
            )
            hit = [c for c in candidates if _name_similarity([name, *aliases], c["names"]) >= NAME_MATCH_MIN][:1]
        entity_id = hit[0]["id"] if hit else _new_id("e")
        self._q(
            """
            MERGE (e:Entity {id: $id})
            ON CREATE SET e.user = $user, e.name = $name, e.kind = $kind, e.created_at = datetime()
            SET e.updated_at = datetime(), e.aliases = [a IN apoc.coll.toSet(coalesce(e.aliases, []) + $aliases) WHERE toLower(a) <> toLower(e.name)],
                e.summary = CASE WHEN $summary <> '' THEN $summary ELSE e.summary END
            WITH e CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(e, 'embedding', $vec)
            """,
            id=entity_id, name=name, kind=kind, aliases=list(aliases), summary=summary, vec=vec,
        )
        return entity_id

    def _lookup(self, name: str, known: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
        """Map a name or id used in a memory/relation to an entity id without creating junk nodes.

        Names resolved in this same extraction win; otherwise an id, then the most recently
        updated entity with that name or alias."""
        key = name.strip().lower()
        if self._is_user(key):
            return self.user
        if key in known:
            return known[key]
        hit = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user})
            WHERE e.id = $n OR toLower(e.name) = $n OR any(a IN coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(a) = $n)
            RETURN e.id AS id ORDER BY CASE WHEN e.id = $n THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, e.updated_at DESC LIMIT 1
            """,
            n=key,
        )
        return hit[0]["id"] if hit else None

    def apply(self, ex: Extraction, episode_id: str | None = None, today: dt.date | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Store one extraction. Returns a human-readable log of what changed."""
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)
        log: list[str] = []
        known: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.forgotten_terms: list[str] = []  # names forgotten by this call (the graph redacts its thread)
        for ent in ex.entities:
            eid = self.resolve_entity(ent.name, ent.kind, ent.aliases, ent.summary, ent.ref, ent.new)
            for n in [ent.name, *ent.aliases, *([ent.ref] if ent.ref else [])]:
                if known.get(n.lower(), eid) != eid:  # two different Sams in one extraction
                    log.append(f"warning: '{n}' names two entities here; references to it go to the last one")
                known[n.lower()] = eid
            if ent.new and not ent.ref:
                log.append(f"new entity {ent.name} ({eid}), distinct from the known {ent.name}")

        # Relations go through the ontology: normalize the type, check its range, then apply
        # its rules (cardinality "one" ends the previous edge; "ended" ends the whole lineage).
        resolved = []
        for rel in ex.relations:
            a, b = self._lookup(rel.source, known), self._lookup(rel.target, known)
            if a and b and a != b:

                if how == "group":
                    log.append(f"rejected {rel.source} -{rel.type}-> {rel.target}: '{rel.type}' is a "

                    continue
                resolved.append((rel, *((b, a) if flip else (a, b)), canon, "flipped" if flip else how))

        # temporary status mentions is a trip, not a move. Applying it would end the real home.

        lasting = {n.lower() for m in ex.memories if m.kind != "status" for n in m.about}
        kept = []
        for item in resolved:
            rel, canon = item[0], item[3]
            target = rel.target.lower()
            if (not rel.ended and ontology.rule(canon, "cardinality") == "one"
                    and target in temporary and target not in lasting):
                log.append(f"ignored {rel.source} -{canon}-> {rel.target}: only a temporary status "
                           "mentions it (a trip, not a move)")
                continue

        for rel, a, b, canon, how in resolved:

                           a=a, b=b)[0]
            src, dst = ("user" if a == self.user else info["a"]), info["b"]
            said = f" (said '{rel.type}')" if how in ("synonym", "flipped") else ""
            if rel.ended:  # breakup, moved away, left a job: keep the edge as history

                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {id: $b})
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )
                if ended:
                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{'/'.join(e['type'] for e in ended)}-> {dst}{said}")
                continue
            if not ontology.range_ok(canon, info["kind"]):
                log.append(f"rejected {src} -{canon}-> {dst}: {canon} needs a {'/'.join(ontology.rule(canon, 'range'))}, "

                continue

                hint = ontology.propose_type(self.driver, canon, f"{src} -{rel.type}-> {dst}")
                log.append(f"new relation type '{canon}' proposed for the ontology (closest: {hint})")

                    """
                    MATCH (a:Entity {id: $a})-[r:RELATED]->(other:Entity)
                    WHERE r.until IS NULL AND r.type IN $types AND (other.id <> $b OR r.type <> $type)
                    SET r.until = $today RETURN other.name AS name, r.type AS type
                    """,
                    a=a, b=b, type=canon, types=sorted(ontology.lineage(canon) | {canon}), today=today,
                )
                for m in moved:
                    log.append(f"ended {src} -{m['type']}-> {m['name']} (one {canon} at a time)")

                MERGE (a)-[r:RELATED {type: $type}]->(b)
                WITH r, r.updated_at IS NULL OR r.until IS NOT NULL AS changed
                SET r.since = coalesce($since, r.since), r.updated_at = $now, r.until = null,
                    r.said = $said_as
                RETURN changed

                a=a, b=b, type=canon, since=rel.since, now=now, said_as=rel.type,
            )[0]["changed"]

                log.append(f"linked {src} -{canon}-> {dst}{said}")

            if q(

                MATCH (m:Memory {id: $id, user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
                SET m.invalidated_at = $now RETURN m.text AS text

            ):
                log.append(f"retired {mid}")

                WHERE node.user = $user AND node.invalidated_at IS NULL AND score >= $min

                  // same dates too: "dentist on 2026-11-12" -> "...on 2026-11-17" reads almost the
                  // same but is a real correction; an identical "replacement" is just a duplicate

                  AND coalesce(node.occurred_on, date('1900-01-01')) = coalesce($occurred, date('1900-01-01'))
                RETURN node.id AS id LIMIT 1

                    """,

                log.append(f"reinforced {dup[0]['id']}")

                    WHERE old.id IN $ids AND old.id <> $keep AND old.invalidated_at IS NULL

                    """,
