tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

"""Lessons 9-10 — MemoryStore: writes memories into the graph and recalls them for a turn.

Write path (Lesson 9):  resolve entities -> link relations -> dedupe -> supersede -> store
Read path  (Lesson 10): core profile + semantic (vector) + entity hop (graph) + follow-ups
                        + recent episodes, ranked by similarity, importance and recency
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import re

import numpy as np

from fastembed import TextEmbedding

from config import COMPANION_NAME, EMBED_MODEL, RERANK_MODEL

_embedder: TextEmbedding | None = None
_reranker = None
_ontology_loaded = False


def embed(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    global _embedder
    _embedder = _embedder or TextEmbedding(EMBED_MODEL)
    return [v.tolist() for v in _embedder.embed(texts)]


def relevance(query: str, texts: list[str]) -> list[float]:
    """How much each text is ABOUT the query, from a cross-encoder (Lesson 18). Unlike an
    embedding, it reads the two together, so "dogs" vs "Mark's son is sick" scores near the
    floor (about -11) while "dogs" vs "Alex has a beagle" scores -5. Logits, not 0-1."""
    global _reranker
    if not texts:
        return []
    if _reranker is None:
        from fastembed.rerank.cross_encoder import TextCrossEncoder
        _reranker = TextCrossEncoder(RERANK_MODEL)
    return [float(s) for s in _reranker.rerank(query, texts)]


def _name_similarity(a: list[str], b: list[str]) -> float:
    """Best cosine similarity between any name/alias in `a` and any in `b`."""
    va, vb = np.array(embed(a)), np.array(embed(b))
    va /= np.linalg.norm(va, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    vb /= np.linalg.norm(vb, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return float((va @ vb.T).max())


def _similar_names(name: str, known: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Another way to say a known name: "Bob" ~ "Robert", "Robert" in "Robert Smith"."""
    words = lambda n: set(re.findall(r"\w+", n.lower()))
    if any(words(name) <= words(k) or words(k) <= words(name) for k in known):
        return True
    return _name_similarity([name], known) >= NAME_MATCH_MIN

        kind: fact | preference | event | plan | feeling | boundary

    (:Memory)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(:Memory)                          newer version of a fact
    (:Memory)-[:FROM]->(:Episode)                               provenance
    (:Episode {id, user, started_at, ended_at, summary, mood, embedding})
    (:Episode)-[:NEXT]->(:Episode), (:Episode)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx, role, text, at})

STATEMENTS = [
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT entity_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT memory_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) REQUIRE m.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT episode_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE INDEX memory_user_kind IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) ON (m.user, m.kind)",
    "CREATE INDEX entity_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) ON (e.user)",
    "CREATE INDEX episode_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) ON (e.user, e.started_at)",
]
for name, label in [("memory_vec", "Memory"), ("entity_vec", "Entity"), ("episode_vec", "Episode")]:
    STATEMENTS.append(
        f"CREATE VECTOR INDEX {name} IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:{label}) ON (n.embedding) "
        f"OPTIONS {{indexConfig: {{`vector.dimensions`: {EMBED_DIMS}, "
        f"`vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}}}"
    )


def ensure_schema(driver) -> None:
    for stmt in STATEMENTS:
        driver.execute_query(stmt)
    driver.execute_query("CALL db.awaitIndexes(120)")

              RETURN m  // boundaries are never private: every persona respects them
              UNION
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
                AND m.kind IN ['fact', 'preference'] AND m.importance >= 6
                AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
              WITH m ORDER BY m.importance DESC, m.created_at DESC LIMIT 8

            WHERE NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)  // sensitive: only as (near) the best match

            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.occurred_on AS occurred_on,

                   round(score, 3) AS score, duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0 AS age

"""Run a query with $user and $now always set ($now: the conversation's clock).

        Inside `_write()` it joins that transaction; otherwise it's its own auto-committed one."""
        params = {"user": self.user, "agent": self.agent, "now": now or clock.now_for(dt.date.today()), **params}
        tx = getattr(self._local, "tx", None)
        if tx is not None:
            return tx.run(query, **params).data()
        records, _, _ = self.driver.execute_query(query, **params)
        return [r.data() for r in records]

    def _write(self, work):
        """Run `work()` as ONE write transaction for this user (Lesson 14).

        - All or nothing: if anything fails half-way, every write rolls back.
        - One writer per user: the first statement writes to the user's node, which takes
          Neo4j's write lock on it until commit. A second writer for the same user (another
          thread or process) waits there, then sees the first one's committed memories, so
          its duplicate check works. Different users never wait for each other.
        - execute_write retries transient errors (deadlocks, leader changes) by running
          `work` again from the start, so `work` must not have side effects outside the graph.
        Nested calls join the outer transaction."""
        if getattr(self._local, "tx", None) is not None:
            return work()

        def unit(tx):
            self._local.tx = tx
            try:
                tx.run("MATCH (u:User {id: $user}) SET u.write_lock = datetime()", user=self.user).consume()
                return work()
            finally:
                self._local.tx = None

        with self.driver.session() as session:
            return session.execute_write(unit)

    def start_episode(self, on: dt.date | None = None) -> str:
        """Open a conversation episode. `on` backdates it (used by the scripted demo)."""
        episode_id = _new_id("ep")

            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.due_on < date($now) - duration({days: $days})
            SET m.status = 'lapsed' RETURN m.text AS text
            """, days=LAPSE_AFTER_DAYS)]

        if writer is not None:
            rows = q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.consolidated_at IS NULL
                  AND m.kind IN ['event', 'status', 'feeling'] AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)
                  AND NOT coalesce(m.private, false)  // a shared pattern must not be built from private memories
                  AND m.created_at > $now - duration({days: $days})
                RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.embedding AS vec ORDER BY m.created_at
                """, days=PATTERN_WINDOW_DAYS)
            for group in _clusters(rows, PATTERN_SIMILARITY, PATTERN_MIN):
                pattern = writer(self.user_name, [r["text"] for r in group], today)
                if pattern is None:

                log += self._write(lambda: self._store_pattern(pattern, group, today, now))

            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE coalesce(ep.summary, '') =~ $re
            RETURN ep.id AS id, ep.summary AS summary

            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, coalesce(e.summary, '') AS summary,
                   coalesce(e.aliases, []) AS aliases

Every similarity cut-off in the memory store (is this a duplicate? the same person? part of a
habit?) was measured on ONE model's scores. Another model spreads its scores differently, so
switching models without re-measuring silently breaks dedupe, entity matching and recall.
A Profile keeps a model and its thresholds together:

    local   BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5    384 dims, on the CPU via fastembed, no key   (default)
    remote  Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B   4096 dims, any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint

for the default, "embedding_qwen3_embedding_8b" + memory_vec_qwen3_embedding_8b for Qwen), so
one database can hold both: the tests run on the local model while your chats use the remote
one, and `python -m companion.reembed` backfills a model's vectors after a switch.

does this message relate to?") and nothing before a stored text. Without it, its separation
of related from unrelated memories fell from 0.99 to 0.90 AUC (lessons/19). So `embed(...,
query=True)` is for a message searched against memories; comparisons between two stored

    sensitive_margin: float   # score: ...and to be within this of the best match
    entity_hop: float         # score: an entity this close to the message is looked up

"""Lesson 19 — measure the similarity thresholds for the active embedding model.

    python -m companion.calibrate               the model in .env (EMBED_MODEL / EMBED_BASE_URL)
    EMBED_BASE_URL= python -m companion.calibrate   the local default, for comparison

Each threshold in companion/embeddings.py answers one yes/no question with a similarity cut.
Below, each question has pairs labelled "yes" and "no". For the active model this prints both
score ranges, how many pairs the profile's current threshold gets right, and the cut that
separates them best (the middle of the gap when there is one). The numbers go into the model's
Profile, then the scenarios (python -m companion.scenarios) check them end to end.

The pairs are cases that went wrong once (the comments in store.py) plus their near misses.
Add the case when you find a new failure: the next model you try will be measured on it too.
"""

import numpy as np

from companion.embeddings import PROFILE, embed

YES, NO = True, False

# (threshold, scale, question, query side?, pairs)
#   scale "score": Neo4j's vector index score (1 + cosine) / 2;  "cosine": raw, in Python
CHECKS = [
    ("duplicate", "score", "Is the new memory a reworded copy of a stored one? (yes: reinforce it)", False, [
        (YES, "Alex's sister Maya lives in Boston", "Maya, Alex's sister, lives in Boston"),

        (YES, "Alex is allergic to peanuts", "Alex has a peanut allergy"),

        (NO, "Alex has a dentist appointment on Tuesday", "Alex has a doctor appointment on Tuesday"),

"""Lesson 19 — measure the similarity thresholds for the active embedding model.

    python -m companion.calibrate               the model in .env (EMBED_MODEL / EMBED_BASE_URL)
    EMBED_BASE_URL= python -m companion.calibrate   the local default, for comparison

Each threshold in companion/embeddings.py answers one yes/no question with a similarity cut.
Below, each question has pairs labelled "yes" and "no". For the active model this prints both
score ranges, how many pairs the profile's current threshold gets right, and the cut that
separates them best (the middle of the gap when there is one). The numbers go into the model's
Profile, then the scenarios (python -m companion.scenarios) check them end to end.

The pairs are cases that went wrong once (the comments in store.py) plus their near misses.
Add the case when you find a new failure: the next model you try will be measured on it too.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from companion.embeddings import PROFILE, embed

YES, NO = True, False

# (threshold, scale, question, query side?, pairs)
#   scale "score": Neo4j's vector index score (1 + cosine) / 2;  "cosine": raw, in Python
CHECKS = [
    ("duplicate", "score", "Is the new memory a reworded copy of a stored one? (yes: reinforce it)", False, [
        (YES, "Alex's sister Maya lives in Boston", "Maya, Alex's sister, lives in Boston"),
        (YES, "Alex works as a nurse", "Alex is a nurse"),
        (YES, "Alex is allergic to peanuts", "Alex has a peanut allergy"),
        (YES, "Alex has a dog named Biscuit", "Alex has a dog called Biscuit"),
        (YES, "Alex enjoys hiking on weekends", "Alex likes to hike on weekends"),
        (YES, "Alex's son Logan is sick", "Logan, Alex's son, is sick"),
        (YES, "Alex prefers tea over coffee", "Alex prefers tea to coffee"),
        (YES, "Alex started a new job at Google", "Alex began a new job at Google"),
        # different facts that read alike: a "reinforce" would lose the new one
        (NO, "Alex's sister Maya lives in Boston", "Alex's sister Maya lives in Seattle"),
        (NO, "Alex's brother is Leo", "Alex's brother is Theo"),
        (NO, "Alex has a dentist appointment on Tuesday", "Alex has a doctor appointment on Tuesday"),
        (NO, "Alex likes coffee", "Alex likes tea"),
        (NO, "Alex went running today", "Alex went swimming today"),
        (NO, "Alex has a dog named Biscuit", "Alex has a cat named Biscuit"),
        (NO, "Alex is a nurse", "Alex's mother is a nurse"),
        (NO, "Alex feels anxious about work", "Alex feels excited about work"),
    ]),
    ("forgotten", "cosine", "Is this the memory the user asked to forget, extracted again?", False, [
        (YES, "Alex's ex Jordan moved to Denver", "Jordan, Alex's ex, moved to Denver"),
        (YES, "Alex is in debt from student loans", "Alex has student loan debt"),
        (YES, "Alex got fired from the bakery", "Alex was fired from the bakery job"),
        (YES, "Alex is seeing a therapist", "Alex sees a therapist"),
        # other things said in the same conversation: must still be stored
        (NO, "Alex's ex Jordan moved to Denver", "Alex is moving to Denver next year"),
        (NO, "Alex is in debt from student loans", "Alex is saving up for a car"),
        (NO, "Alex got fired from the bakery", "Alex starts a new job at the library"),
        (NO, "Alex is seeing a therapist", "Alex's sister is a therapist"),
    ]),
    ("entity_match", "score", "Is this entity (different name) the same one as a known entity?", False, [
        (YES, "Mom (person): Alex's mother, lives in Ohio", "my mother (person): Alex's mother who lives in Ohio"),
        (YES, "NYC (place): the city where Alex works", "New York (place): the city Alex works in"),
        (YES, "Bob (person): Alex's coworker at the bank", "Robert (person): Alex's coworker at the bank"),
        (YES, "Dad (person): Alex's father", "father (person): Alex's dad"),
        (NO, "Seattle (place): the city where Riley now lives", "Boston (place): the city where Riley lives"),
        (NO, "Sam (person): Alex's coworker", "Jordan (person): Alex's coworker"),
        (NO, "Biscuit (pet): Alex's dog", "Pepper (pet): Alex's dog"),
        (NO, "Maya (person): Alex's sister", "Mia (person): Alex's sister's friend"),
    ]),
    ("name_match", "cosine", "Are these two names for the same thing?", False, [
        (YES, "Mom", "mother"), (YES, "my mother", "Mom"), (YES, "NYC", "New York"),
        (YES, "Bob", "Robert"), (YES, "Dad", "father"), (YES, "Liz", "Elizabeth"), (YES, "Mike", "Michael"),
        (NO, "Seattle", "Boston"), (NO, "Sam", "Jordan"), (NO, "Maya", "Mia"),
        (NO, "Biscuit", "Pepper"), (NO, "Leo", "Theo"), (NO, "Ohio", "Iowa"),
    ]),
    ("pattern", "cosine", "Are these two memories the same habit?", False, [
        (YES, "Riley is heading to the gym", "Riley just got back from the gym."),
        (YES, "Riley is at the gym before work.", "Riley is going to the gym after work and then having dinner"),
        (YES, "Riley's legs feel exhausted after a gym session.", "Riley is heading to the gym"),
        (YES, "Pytest is at the gym", "Pytest is heading to the gym for leg day"),
        (YES, "Alex went for a run this morning", "Alex is out running"),
        (NO, "Riley is heading to the gym", "Riley went rock climbing"),
        (NO, "Riley is at the gym before work.", "Riley went hiking with friends"),
        (NO, "Pytest is at the gym", "Pytest had pizza for dinner"),
        (NO, "Alex went for a run this morning", "Alex went to a yoga class"),
    ]),
    ("sensitive_floor", "score", "Is the message about this sensitive memory? (yes: recall it)", True, [
        (YES, "my meds aren't helping", "Alex has ADHD and takes medication for it"),
        (YES, "I'm stressed about money this month", "Alex is in credit card debt"),
        (YES, "therapy is tomorrow and I'm nervous", "Alex sees a therapist for depression"),
        (YES, "can't focus at all today", "Alex has ADHD and takes medication for it"),
        (NO, "what should I cook tonight?", "Alex has ADHD and takes medication for it"),
        (NO, "dogs", "Alex is in credit card debt"),
        (NO, "the weather is great today", "Alex sees a therapist for depression"),
        (NO, "I watched a movie last night", "Alex is in credit card debt"),
    ]),
    ("entity_hop", "score", "Does the message mean this entity (without naming it)?", True, [
        (YES, "how is my kid doing?", "Logan (person): Alex's son"),
        (YES, "my mom called me today", "Linda (person): Alex's mother"),
        (YES, "work was rough today", "Acme (organization): the company where Alex works"),
        (YES, "the dog chewed my shoes", "Biscuit (pet): Alex's dog"),
        (NO, "dogs", "Logan (person): Alex's son"),
        (NO, "what's the weather like?", "Acme (organization): the company where Alex works"),
        (NO, "I had pasta for lunch", "Linda (person): Alex's mother"),
        (NO, "I'm tired", "Biscuit (pet): Alex's dog"),
    ]),
]


def similarity(a: str, b: str, query: bool, scale: str) -> float:
    va = np.array(embed([a], query=query)[0])
    vb = np.array(embed([b])[0])
    cos = float(va @ vb)
    return (1 + cos) / 2 if scale == "score" else cos


def best_cut(yes: list[float], no: list[float]) -> float:
    """The middle of the gap if the two sets separate; else the cut with the fewest mistakes."""
    if min(yes) > max(no):
        return (min(yes) + max(no)) / 2
    cuts = sorted(yes + no)
    return max(cuts, key=lambda c: sum(y >= c for y in yes) + sum(n < c for n in no))


def main() -> None:
    print(f"Model: {PROFILE.model} ({PROFILE.dims} dims)\n")
    suggested = {}
    for name, scale, question, query, pairs in CHECKS:
        yes = [similarity(a, b, query, scale) for ok, a, b in pairs if ok]
        no = [similarity(a, b, query, scale) for ok, a, b in pairs if not ok]
        now = getattr(PROFILE, name)
        right = sum(y >= now for y in yes) + sum(n < now for n in no)
        cut = best_cut(yes, no)
        gap = min(yes) - max(no)
        suggested[name] = round(cut, 3)
        print(f"{name}  ({scale}{', query side' if query else ''})  {question}")
        print(f"  yes {min(yes):.3f}-{max(yes):.3f}   no {min(no):.3f}-{max(no):.3f}   "
              f"{'gap' if gap > 0 else 'overlap'} {abs(gap):.3f}")
        print(f"  current {now}: {right}/{len(pairs)} right   suggested {cut:.3f}")
        for ok, a, b in pairs:  # the pairs the current threshold gets wrong
            s = similarity(a, b, query, scale)
            if (s >= now) != ok:
                print(f"    wrong: {s:.3f} {'yes' if ok else 'no '}  {a!r} ~ {b!r}")
        print()
    print("Suggested:", ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in suggested.items()))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

p='companion/embeddings.py'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1,old; s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''    query_instruction: str = ""  # put before a query (not before stored text)
''','''    query_instruction: str = ""    # put before a query (not before stored text)
    cluster_instruction: str = ""  # put before memories grouped into habits (Lesson 13)
''')
rep('''            query_instruction="Instruct: Given a message from a user, retrieve memories about the "
                              "user's life that it relates to\\nQuery: "),''','''            query_instruction="Instruct: Given a message from a user, retrieve memories about the "
                              "user's life that it relates to\\nQuery: ",
            # without it, "heading to the gym" vs "went rock climbing" (0.77) outscored two
            # gym sentences (0.73): complete-linkage clustering couldn't find the habit
            cluster_instruction="Instruct: Identify the activity or habit described\\nQuery: "),''')
rep('''_cache: OrderedDict[tuple[bool, str], np.ndarray] = OrderedDict()  # (query?, text) -> unit vector''',
    '''_cache: OrderedDict[tuple[str, str], np.ndarray] = OrderedDict()  # (instruction, text) -> unit vector''')
start=s.index('def embed(texts')
s=s[:start]+'''def embed(texts: list[str], query: bool = False) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Unit-length vectors (so a dot product is the cosine). `query=True`: the text is a message
    searched against stored memories/entities, and gets the model's query instruction."""
    return _embed(texts, PROFILE.query_instruction if query else "")


def embed_for_clustering(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Vectors for grouping memories into habits. Not stored: consolidation embeds again
    when the model has a clustering instruction, else it can use the stored vectors."""
    return _embed(texts, PROFILE.cluster_instruction)


def _embed(texts: list[str], instruction: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    keys = [(instruction, t) for t in texts]
    found: dict[tuple[str, str], np.ndarray] = {}
    with _lock:
        for k in keys:
            if k in _cache:
                found[k] = _cache[k]
                _cache.move_to_end(k)
    missing = [k for k in dict.fromkeys(keys) if k not in found]
    if missing:
        vecs = _compute([i + t for i, t in missing])
        vecs /= np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        found.update(zip(missing, vecs))

"""Lesson 19 — give every stored memory, entity and episode a vector from the active model.

    python -m companion.reembed              nodes that don't have one yet (after a switch)
    python -m companion.reembed --all        recompute every vector (e.g. a changed instruction)
    python -m companion.reembed --user Mark  one user only

Run it after changing EMBED_MODEL / EMBED_BASE_URL. Each model writes its own property
(embedding / embedding_<model>), so the old vectors stay and switching back costs nothing.
The text embedded is the same text the write path embeds (keep them in step: a vector made
from different text matches differently). Tombstones (:Forgotten) keep no text, so they
can't be re-embedded; they only matter while their episode is open, so that's harmless.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time

from neo4j import GraphDatabase

from config import NEO4J_AUTH, NEO4J_URI
from companion.embeddings import PROFILE, embed, remote
from companion.schema import ensure_schema

    "Entity": "n.name + ' (' + n.kind + '): ' + coalesce(n.summary, '')",
    "Memory": "n.text",
    "Episode": "n.summary",
}
BATCH = 64

            where.append("NOT n:User")
        if user:
            where.append("n.user = $user")

"""Lesson 19 — choosing an embedding model: profiles, query instructions, re-embedding.

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_19_embeddings.py -v

These run on the local model (conftest.py sets that up), and a fake endpoint stands in for the
remote one, so they check the wiring without an API key. Whether a remote model's thresholds
are RIGHT is what `python -m companion.calibrate` and the scenarios measure.
"""
import numpy as np
import pytest

from companion import calibrate, embeddings
from companion.embeddings import PROFILES, Profile, embed, profile_for
from companion.models import Extraction, MemoryOut
from companion.schema import vector_indexes

QWEN = PROFILES["Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B"]


def test_the_default_model_keeps_the_names_lessons_8_to_18_use():
    local = profile_for("BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")
    assert (local.prop, local.index("memory_vec")) == ("embedding", "memory_vec")
    assert embeddings.PROFILE == local  # conftest: the tests run on the local model


def test_another_model_gets_its_own_property_and_indexes():
    assert QWEN.prop == "embedding_qwen3_embedding_8b"
    stmts = " ".join(vector_indexes(QWEN))
    assert "memory_vec_qwen3_embedding_8b" in stmts and "n.embedding_qwen3_embedding_8b" in stmts
    assert "`vector.dimensions`: 4096" in stmts  # an index has ONE size: 384 and 4096 can't share


def test_a_model_without_measured_thresholds_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="calibrate"):
        profile_for("some/new-model")


@pytest.fixture
def fake_remote(monkeypatch):
    """The Qwen profile with a fake endpoint that records what it was sent."""
    sent = []

    def compute(texts):
        sent.append(list(texts))
        return np.array([[len(t), 1.0, 0.0] for t in texts], dtype=np.float32)

    monkeypatch.setattr(embeddings, "PROFILE", QWEN)
    monkeypatch.setattr(embeddings, "_compute", compute)
    monkeypatch.setattr(embeddings, "_cache", type(embeddings._cache)())
    return sent


def test_a_query_gets_the_instruction_and_stored_text_does_not(fake_remote):
    embed(["Logan has a fever"])
    embed(["how is my kid?"], query=True)
    stored, query = fake_remote
    assert stored == ["Logan has a fever"]
    assert query[0].startswith("Instruct: ") and query[0].endswith("how is my kid?")


def test_vectors_are_unit_length_and_cached(fake_remote):
    a = embed(["Mom", "Mom", "mother"])
    assert fake_remote == [["Mom", "mother"]]  # one call, each text once
    assert embed(["mother"]) == [a[2]] and len(fake_remote) == 1  # from the cache
    assert embed(["mother"], query=True) and len(fake_remote) == 2  # a query is a different vector
    assert all(abs(np.linalg.norm(v) - 1) < 1e-6 for v in a)


def test_clustering_uses_its_own_instruction(fake_remote):
    embeddings.embed_for_clustering(["Riley is at the gym"])
    assert fake_remote[0][0].startswith("Instruct: Identify the activity")


def test_the_local_thresholds_hold_on_the_calibration_pairs():
    """The pairs calibrate.py measures a new model on also pin down the current one. These
    three thresholds decide alone; entity matching and sensitive recall have a second check
    (names, the margin to the best match), so a single cut isn't expected to be perfect."""
    p = embeddings.PROFILE
    for name, scale, _, side, pairs in calibrate.CHECKS:
        if name in ("duplicate", "forgotten", "name_match"):
            wrong = [(a, b) for ok, a, b in pairs
                     if (calibrate.similarity(a, b, side, scale) >= getattr(p, name)) != ok]
            assert not wrong, f"{name}: {wrong}"


def test_best_cut_is_the_middle_of_the_gap():
    assert calibrate.best_cut([0.9, 0.95], [0.5, 0.7]) == pytest.approx(0.8)


def test_reembed_fills_in_missing_vectors_and_recall_finds_them_again(store, driver):
    from companion.reembed import reembed

    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[MemoryOut(text="Pytest's son Logan has a fever", kind="event", importance=6)]))
    store._q("MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) REMOVE m.embedding")  # as if made by another model
    assert store.recall("how is Logan feeling?")["semantic"] == []

    counts = reembed(driver, user="pytest")
    assert counts["Memory"] == 1 and counts["User"] == 0  # only what was missing
    assert [m["text"] for m in store.recall("how is Logan feeling?")["semantic"]] == ["Pytest's son Logan has a fever"]


def test_a_tombstone_from_another_model_is_ignored(store):
    store._q("CREATE (:Forgotten {user: $user, episode: 'ep_x'})")  # no vector for this model
    assert store._tombstones("ep_x") == []

**Architecture:** component, LangGraph, sequence, data-model and lifecycle diagrams for the
agent and the companion are in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## LLM settings (lessons 5 and 7–18)

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling works (OpenAI, DeepInfra, OpenRouter,
Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM...). Set in `.env`:

| Key | |
|---|---|
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `http://localhost:11434/v1` |
| `LLM_MODEL` | chat model name |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | key (any value for local servers) |
| `LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL` | optional, model for memory extraction (defaults to `LLM_MODEL`) |
| `LLM_TEMPERATURE` | chat temperature |
| `COMPANION_USER`, `COMPANION_NAME` | default user and companion names |

Embeddings run locally (`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` via fastembed), no key needed. So does the
reranker that labels unrelated recall matches (`RERANK_MODEL`, default
`Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, Lesson 18). Both are downloaded once and loaded once per process.

## Files

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` | Neo4j 5.26 with APOC + GDS, data in named volumes |
| `.env.example` → `.env` | Neo4j credentials and LLM keys (`.env` is git-ignored) |
| `config.py` | Loads `.env` for the scripts |
| `seed/00_seed.cypher` | Starting graph for Lesson 1 |
| `team_graph.py` | Lesson 4 — Python driver patterns |
| `embed.py` | Lesson 5 — local embeddings + vector index |
| `graphrag.py` | Lesson 5 — GraphRAG retrieval (+ LLM answer via the OpenAI SDK if `LLM_*` is set) |
| `team_agent.py` | Lesson 7 — LangGraph agent with graph tools |
| `companion/` | Lessons 8–10 — memory schema, store, extraction, LangGraph companion, CLI, demo |
| `companion/scenarios.py` | Lessons 11–12 — multi-session scenario tests for memory |
| `companion/ontology.py` | Lesson 12 — relation-type ontology: vocabulary, rules, inference |
| `companion/clock.py`, `companion/decay.py` | Lesson 13 — one clock; the forgetting curve |
| `companion/worker.py` | Lesson 14 — background extraction worker |
| `companion/insights.py` | Lesson 15 — graph embeddings (FastRP + kNN) and node similarity |
| `companion/web.py`, `companion/static/` | Lessons 17–18 — web UI (FastAPI + one HTML page) and the per-turn memory trace |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Architecture diagrams (Mermaid) for lessons 7–17 |
| `tests/`, `pytest.ini` | Per-lesson tests and LLM evals (see *Tests and evals*) |
| `docs/glossary.md` | Glossary of overlapping memory / graph / ontology terms |
| `lessons/outputs/` | Recorded runs for lessons 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 17 |

## Tests and evals

Every lesson has tests in [`tests/`](tests), named after it (`test_05_vectors_and_graphrag.py`).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest                    # unit + database tests: seconds, free (default)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m "not db and not llm"   # unit tests only, no Neo4j needed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m llm             # LLM evals: real calls, cost money
EVAL_TRIALS=3 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -m llm tests/test_11_extraction_evals.py   # pass rates
```

A `-m` on the command line *replaces* the default `-m "not llm"` in `pytest.ini`, so spell
out `and not llm` when you add your own filter. Database tests never leave data behind: writes run in rolled-back transactions, and memory
tests use their own `pytest` user. A test for a lesson you haven't done yet is skipped with a
reason. [Lesson 0](lessons/00-setup.md#test-it) explains the three kinds of test, and each
lesson ends with a *Test it* section on what its tests teach.

## Common commands

```bash
docker compose ps                 # status / health
docker compose logs -f neo4j      # logs
docker compose stop               # stop, keep data
docker compose down -v            # stop and DELETE all data
.venv/bin/python team_agent.py    # Lesson 7 agent (interactive)
.venv/bin/python -m companion     # companion chat (/help for commands; --persona Coach, --sync)
.venv/bin/python -m companion.web # Lessons 17-18 web UI on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (click a reply to see its trace)
.venv/bin/python -m companion.demo   # scripted two-session companion demo
.venv/bin/python -m companion.scenarios   # Lesson 11–16 scenario tests (real LLM calls)
.venv/bin/python graphrag.py "Who should own our new Rust performance work?"
```

## Test it — [`tests/test_18_inspect.py`](../tests/test_18_inspect.py)

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_18_inspect.py -v    # 8 tests, ~4 s, no LLM
```

A trace that is wrong teaches the wrong thing, so it gets tests like any other feature:

- a turn records the recall, the prompt (with `<memories>`), timings and decisions with reasons;
- the second mention is `reinforced` with its similarity, the old memory was a candidate, and
  Miso is highlighted;
- small talk shows *skipped* and why;
- (in [`test_10_recall.py`](../tests/test_10_recall.py)) "do you like pizza?" gets only
  weak matches; "my dog hates storms" keeps the dog on top; "my meds don't help" still reaches
  the ADHD memory in the prompt, though the reranker scored it weak;
- the recall preview doesn't change `access_count`;
- looking 90 days ahead halves an event's strength and expires "tired today", without writing anything;
- the persona lens hides Sage's private Dr. Lee from Coach;
- the diary lists the open episode with its turns and memories;
- the reasons come from `MemoryStore`, so they're in the terminal too.

## Takeaways

- Show the **read** as well as the write. Most "why did it say that?" questions are answered
  by what recall returned, not by what was stored.
- Record the trace **where the work happens** (the graph nodes) instead of recomputing it for
  display. A second recall could return something different from what the model saw.
- Every decision should carry its **reason and its number**. Thresholds stop being magic once
  you can see a 0.971 that just missed.
- Inspection must be **read-only**: a preview that bumps access counts changes what it measures.
- Vector search can't say "nothing found". Measure related vs unrelated scores before picking a
  cut-off. When the signals overlap, **don't drop, and don't tell the model either**: hiding a
  related memory, or calling it unrelated, costs more than showing a weak one to a model that
  can judge it. Show the score where a person reads it (the trace).

## Next

That's the end of the course. A good place to keep going: the reasons and timings in the trace are
what you'd send to tracing tools like LangSmith or OpenTelemetry in production.
# Lesson 18: watching memory work, one turn at a time

Lesson 17's page shows what memory **holds**: the graph, the decay curves and the related pairs. Each turn
also does two things you can't see from the result:

- a **read**: recall picks a few memories, and they become text in the prompt;
- a **write**: extraction proposes memories, and the store keeps, merges or drops each one.

This lesson makes both visible. Click any reply in the chat and the right-hand side shows
what memory did for that reply.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m companion.web        # http://127.0.0.1:8000, then click a reply
```

| Tab | Shows | Teaches |
|---|---|---|
| **This turn** | timings, everything recall found grouped by retriever, the extraction's decisions with reasons | the read path (Lesson 10) and the write path (Lesson 9) |
| **Prompt** | the exact system prompt, with the memory block highlighted, plus token counts | the model is stateless: "memory" is text rebuilt every turn |
| **Life graph** | what this turn's recall touched, highlighted; a **Seen by** switch for the other persona | graph hops; private vs. shared (Lesson 16) |
| **Strength** | a **Look ahead** slider, 0–365 days | decay, dormancy and expiry (Lesson 13) |
| **Try recall** | recall for any text, on any date, as either persona, without chatting | how recall changes with wording, time and persona |
| **Diary** | episodes (turns, memories taken from each, summary) and consolidated patterns | episodes (Lesson 11) and consolidation (Lesson 13) |

to the current turn's entry as it runs:

"""Compare embedding models: do related and unrelated messages separate by best-match score?"""
import sys, time, json
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/markcastillo/git/neo4j-graph-tutorial")
import config
from openai import OpenAI
from neo4j import GraphDatabase

d = GraphDatabase.driver(config.NEO4J_URI, auth=config.NEO4J_AUTH)
texts = lambda u: [r["t"] for r in d.execute_query("MATCH (m:Memory {user:$u}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL RETURN m.text AS t", u=u).records]
MEM = {"mark": texts("user:mark"), "alex": texts("user:alex (demo)"),
       "riley": ["Riley was diagnosed with ADHD in 2025 and takes medication for it.",
                 "Riley loves hiking and Forest Park is their favorite place to do so.",
                 "Riley signed up for the Chicago half marathon in March 2027",
                 "Riley lives in Portland.", "Riley's sister Maya is a nurse in Denver."]}
REL = {"mark": ["how is my son doing?", "is Logan feeling better?", "I called the school", "what do you remember about my kid?", "Logan's school"],
       "alex": ["dogs", "how's Biscuit?", "where do I live?", "how did my presentation go?", "is my sister visiting?", "what's my job?",
                "I'm nervous about Thursday", "my puppy chewed my shoes", "I'm dreading standing up in front of the execs"],
       "riley": ["I'm struggling to focus at work, my meds don't seem to help", "I can't concentrate on anything lately",
                 "should I go for a walk in the woods this weekend?", "Can you help me plan my training for this week?",
                 "how many miles should I run this week?"]}
UNREL = {"mark": ["dogs", "what's the weather like?", "I love pizza", "tell me a joke", "my car broke down", "hi", "work was stressful", "I'm bored"],
         "alex": ["tell me a joke", "my car broke down", "I love pizza", "what's the weather like?", "I bought new shoes", "my back hurts"],
         "riley": ["tell me a joke", "I bought new shoes", "my car broke down", "what's the weather like?"]}

client = OpenAI(base_url=config.LLM_BASE_URL, api_key=REDACTED, timeout=60)
QWEN_INSTR = "Instruct: Given a message from a user, retrieve memories about the user's life that it relates to\nQuery: "

def remote(model, qprefix="", pprefix=""):
    def f(xs, query):
        p = qprefix if query else pprefix
        r = client.embeddings.create(model=model, input=[p + x for x in xs], encoding_format="float")
        return np.array([e.embedding for e in r.data])
    return f

def local():
    from fastembed import TextEmbedding
    m = TextEmbedding(config.EMBED_MODEL)
    return lambda xs, query: np.array(list(m.embed(xs)))

MODELS = {
    "local bge-small-en-v1.5": local(),
    "BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5": remote("BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5", "Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: "),
    "intfloat/e5-large-v2": remote("intfloat/e5-large-v2", "query: ", "passage: "),
    "thenlper/gte-large": remote("thenlper/gte-large"),
    "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B": remote("Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B", QWEN_INSTR),
    "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B": remote("Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B", QWEN_INSTR),
    "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B": remote("Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B", QWEN_INSTR),
}
only = sys.argv[1:]
for name, emb in MODELS.items():
    if only and not any(o in name for o in only):
        continue
    try:
        t0 = time.time()
        P = {u: emb(t, False) for u, t in MEM.items()}
        rows = []
        for u in MEM:
            for q, r in [(q, 1) for q in REL[u]] + [(q, 0) for q in UNREL[u]]:
                v = emb([q], True)[0]
                sims = (P[u] / np.linalg.norm(P[u], axis=1, keepdims=True)) @ (v / np.linalg.norm(v))
                rows.append((r, u, q, float(sims.max()), MEM[u][int(sims.argmax())][:45]))
        secs = time.time() - t0
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"== {name}: FAILED {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:150]}"); continue
    rel = sorted(x for x in rows if x[0]); un = sorted((x for x in rows if not x[0]), key=lambda x: x[3])
    # AUC: chance a random related message outscores a random unrelated one
    auc = np.mean([a[3] > b[3] for a in rel for b in un])
    best_cut = max(((sum(a[3] >= c for a in rel) + sum(b[3] < c for b in un)), c) for c in sorted(x[3] for x in rows))
    dims = P["mark"].shape[1]
    print(f"== {name}  dims {dims}  {secs:.1f}s  AUC {auc:.3f}  best single cut {best_cut[1]:.3f} -> {best_cut[0]}/{len(rows)} right")
    print("   lowest related: ", [(round(x[3], 3), x[2][:30]) for x in sorted(rel, key=lambda x: x[3])[:4]])
    print("   highest unrelated:", [(round(x[3], 3), x[2][:30]) for x in un[-4:]])
    sys.stdout.flush()

# Lesson 19: choosing an embedding model (and re-measuring everything that depends on it)

Since Lesson 8, the companion has embedded memories with `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`: 384
dimensions on the CPU, no key. Lesson 18's **Try recall** tab showed its limit. "dogs" returned
"Mark's son is sick" with almost the same score as a real match. That's because small models
squeeze every score into a narrow band. This lesson swaps in a bigger remote model. Doing that
safely means more than changing a model name:

1. **Measure** which model separates related from unrelated memories best, on your own data.
2. **Re-measure every threshold**: eight cut-offs in the store were tuned on bge-small's scores.
3. **Keep the vectors apart**: one index has one size, and tests shouldn't need an API key.
4. **Backfill**: memories stored before the switch have no vector from the new model.

```bash
# .env
EMBED_BASE_URL=https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai   # any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint
EMBED_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B
# EMBED_API_KEY defaults to LLM_API_KEY

.venv/bin/python -m companion.reembed      # give existing memories a Qwen vector
.venv/bin/python -m companion.web          # same app, new embeddings
```

Leave `EMBED_BASE_URL` empty and everything runs on bge-small, as before.

## 1. Pick a model by measuring, not by leaderboard

The question recall asks: *does this message's best-matching memory score higher when the
message is related than when it isn't?* We wrote 19 related messages ("how is my son doing?",
"my puppy chewed my shoes", "my meds don't seem to help") and 18 unrelated ones ("dogs" for
someone with no dog, "tell me a joke", "my car broke down") against three users' real
memories. For each model we computed the **AUC**: the chance that a random related message
outscores a random unrelated one (0.5 = coin flip, 1.0 = perfect).

| Model | Dims | Where | AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 | 384 | local CPU | 0.854 |
| intfloat/e5-large-v2 | 1024 | DeepInfra | 0.681 |
| thenlper/gte-large | 1024 | DeepInfra | 0.942 |
| BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 | 1024 | DeepInfra | 0.956 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B | 2560 | DeepInfra | 0.962 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | 1024 | DeepInfra | 0.974 |
| **Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B** | **4096** | DeepInfra | **0.994** |

Three things to notice:

- **Bigger isn't monotonic.** The 4B scored below the 0.6B on this set. Leaderboards average
  over many tasks; yours is one task. Measure it.
- **e5-large scored the worst** despite being a well-known model, because e5 needs `query: ` and
  `passage: ` prefixes and is sensitive to them. A model's usage notes are part of the model.
- **The instruction matters.** Qwen3-Embedding is trained to read an instruction before a
  *query* and nothing before a stored text. Without the instruction, the 8B fell from 0.994 to
  about 0.90.

With Qwen3-8B, a single cut-off got 36 of 37 messages right. bge-small couldn't do that at any
cut-off, and that's why Lesson 18 had to add a cross-encoder.

## 2. Query vs. stored text — [`companion/embeddings.py`](../companion/embeddings.py)

```python
embed(["Logan has a fever"])               # stored text: as is
embed(["how is my kid?"], query=True)      # a message searched against memories:
                                           # "Instruct: Given a message from a user, retrieve
                                           #  memories about the user's life...\nQuery: how is my kid?"
```

Which side is which:

| Comparison | Embedded as |
|---|---|
| message → memories (recall, extraction candidates) | query → stored |
| message → entities (the graph hop) | query → stored |
| new memory → stored memory (dedupe), tombstone | stored ↔ stored |
| entity → entity (same person?), name ↔ name | stored ↔ stored |
| memory ↔ memory (habits, Lesson 13) | both with a *clustering* instruction |

The last row was a surprise, and it's covered under step 3. bge-small has no instructions, so all
three calls are the same for it.

`embed()` also normalizes every vector to length 1, so a dot product is the cosine. It keeps a
small cache, because one extraction embeds the same names and summaries several times and a
remote call takes about 0.3–0.6 s.

## 3. Every threshold belongs to a model — [`companion/calibrate.py`](../companion/calibrate.py)

The store makes eight yes/no decisions with a similarity cut-off. Each was measured on
bge-small (the comments in `store.py` keep those measurements). Qwen spreads its scores
differently, so a value that worked for bge-small is wrong for Qwen, and the result fails
quietly: duplicates pile up, two people merge into one, or a habit is never noticed.

So each model has a **Profile** with its own numbers:

```python
Profile("Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B", dims=4096, duplicate=0.966, forgotten=0.89, entity_match=0.94,
        name_match=0.84, pattern=0.665, sensitive_floor=0.655, sensitive_margin=0.015,
        entity_hop=0.62, query_instruction=..., cluster_instruction=...)
```

A model without a profile is refused at startup, with a message pointing here. The numbers
come from `calibrate.py`, which holds labelled pairs for each decision. They're the cases that
went wrong once, plus near misses:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m companion.calibrate                    # the model in .env
EMBED_BASE_URL= .venv/bin/python -m companion.calibrate    # bge-small, for comparison
```

```
duplicate  (score, text)  Is the new memory a reworded copy of a stored one? (yes: reinforce it)
  yes 0.977-0.997   no 0.889-0.956   gap 0.021
  current 0.966: 16/16 right   suggested 0.966
```

What the two models showed:

| Decision | Scale | bge-small: yes / no | Qwen3-8B: yes / no | Qwen value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| duplicate (reworded copy) | score | 0.983+ / ≤ 0.964 | 0.977+ / ≤ 0.956 | 0.966 |
| forgotten (tombstone) | cosine | 0.978+ / ≤ 0.887 | 0.925+ / ≤ 0.858 | 0.89 |
| entity match (same kind) | score | 0.986+ / ≤ 0.946 | 0.949+ / ≤ 0.933 | 0.94 |
| name match ("Mom" ~ "mother") | cosine | 0.803+ / ≤ 0.681 | 0.768+ / ≤ 0.854 overlap | 0.84 |
| pattern (same habit) | cosine | 0.805+ / ≤ 0.803 | 0.682+ / ≤ 0.645 (with instruction) | 0.665 |
| sensitive floor | score | 0.762+ / ≤ 0.737 | 0.695+ / ≤ 0.615 | 0.655 |
| entity hop ("my kid" → Logan) | score | 0.760+ / ≤ 0.731 | 0.645+ / ≤ 0.592 | 0.62 |

Here's what the table says:

- **The better model's scores are lower, not higher.** Qwen puts unrelated pairs far below
  related ones. Floors set for bge-small (0.72, 0.85) would cut off most of Qwen's real matches.
- **The entity hop never worked on bge-small.** Its threshold of 0.85 sits above every
  implicit mention (0.76–0.81), so "how is my kid?" only found Logan through other routes. With
  Qwen at 0.62, the hop finds him. A threshold can look fine for months while it's doing
  nothing, and measuring it is how you find out.
- **Bare names are Qwen's weak spot.** "Ohio" ~ "Iowa" scores 0.854 and "Liz" ~ "Elizabeth"
  scores 0.768. That's tolerable because the name check never decides alone: it runs only after
  the entity match, and nicknames usually arrive as aliases from the extractor.
- **Habits needed their own instruction.** Without one, "heading to the gym" vs. "went rock
  climbing" scored 0.77, higher than two gym sentences (0.73). Complete-linkage clustering
  (Lesson 13) then can't find the habit at any cut-off. With *"Identify the activity or habit
  described"* in front of every memory, the gym sentences score 0.68 or more and climbing
  scores 0.65 or less. Consolidation embeds again with that instruction (the vectors aren't
  stored).

None of the calibration pairs prove the numbers are right on their own. The scenarios
(`python -m companion.scenarios`) run the whole companion with the new profile, end to end.

## 4. Two models, one database

A Neo4j vector index has **one size**, so 384-dim and 4096-dim vectors can't share one. Each
model writes its own property and has its own indexes:

| Model | Property | Indexes |
|---|---|---|
| bge-small (default) | `embedding` | `memory_vec`, `entity_vec`, `episode_vec` |
| Qwen3-Embedding-8B | `embedding_qwen3_embedding_8b` | `memory_vec_qwen3_embedding_8b`, ... |

The Cypher takes both as parameters, which `MemoryStore._q` fills in on every query:

```cypher
CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes($memory_vec, 50, $vec) YIELD node, score ...
CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(m, $vprop, $vec)
RETURN m[$vprop] AS vec
```

This gives three things:

- **The tests stay local.** `tests/conftest.py` empties `EMBED_BASE_URL` before `.env` loads.
  The test suite runs offline in seconds, pins bge-small's thresholds, and doesn't touch the
  vectors your chats use. `TEST_REMOTE_EMBEDDINGS=1` opts in to the remote model.
- **Switching back costs nothing.** The old vectors are still there.
- **Lessons 5–7** (`embed.py`, `graphrag.py`, `team_agent.py`) keep `LOCAL_EMBED_MODEL` and
  their own 384-dim index.

## 5. Backfill — [`companion/reembed.py`](../companion/reembed.py)

Memories stored before the switch have no Qwen vector, so vector search can't see them.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m companion.reembed              # only nodes missing a vector for this model
.venv/bin/python -m companion.reembed --all        # all of them (e.g. after changing an instruction)
.venv/bin/python -m companion.reembed --user Mark
```

It embeds the **same text the write path embeds**: `"Logan (person): Mark's son"` for an entity
and `"Mark, the user"` for the user node. A vector built from different text would match
differently from one the store writes later.

One kind of node can't be backfilled: a `/forget` tombstone keeps only its vector, never the
text. Those matter only while their episode is open, so a tombstone from before a switch is
ignored (`_tombstones` skips nodes without this model's vector).

## Cost and speed

| | bge-small (local) | Qwen3-8B (DeepInfra) |
|---|---|---|
| one call | ~5 ms | ~300–600 ms |
| per turn | recall + extraction: a handful of calls | the same calls, cached repeats are free |
| storage per vector | 1.5 KB | 16 KB |
| price | free | about $0.01 per million tokens |
| offline | yes | no |

Recall now waits on one remote call per turn. In the web UI's trace, `recall_ms` grows by
roughly the call time. For a companion that's fine. For a hot path you'd batch calls or run a
smaller model locally.

## Test it — [`tests/test_19_embeddings.py`](../tests/test_19_embeddings.py)

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_19_embeddings.py -v    # 10 tests, ~1 s, no key
```

A fake endpoint stands in for the remote model. The tests check that:

- the default model keeps the property and index names Lessons 8–18 use, and Qwen gets its own
  4096-dim indexes;
- a model with no measured thresholds is refused;
- a query gets the instruction and stored text doesn't; clustering uses its own instruction;
- vectors are unit length, and repeats come from the cache;
- the local profile gets every `duplicate`, `forgotten` and `name_match` calibration pair right;
- `reembed` fills in a missing vector, and recall finds that memory again;
- a tombstone with no vector for this model is ignored, not a crash.

## Takeaways

- **Thresholds belong to the model**, not to the code. Keep them together (a profile), and
  refuse a model that hasn't been measured.
- **Measure on your own task.** Neither size nor reputation predicted the ranking here.
- **Read the model's usage notes**: query instructions and prefixes changed results more than
  the choice between models did.
- **Keep labelled pairs for every cut-off**, and add each new failure to them. The next model
  is then measured on everything that ever went wrong.
- **Version vectors by model**, so tests, rollbacks and migrations don't fight over one index.

## Next

That's the end of the course. A good place to keep going: try `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`. It
scored 0.974 at a quarter of the size, so you'd add its profile and run the calibration and
the scenarios.

content.content:
## Retrieval

| Term | Meaning | In this repo | Often confused with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Embedding** | A vector representing meaning | `bge-small`, 384 dims | a graph embedding (structure, e.g. `gds.fastRP`) |
| **Cosine similarity** | Angle-based vector similarity | Neo4j's vector score is cosine *rescaled* to 0–1: (1 + cos) / 2 | distance |
| **ANN / HNSW** | Approximate nearest-neighbour search / the graph-based index Neo4j's vector index uses | `db.index.vector.queryNodes` | exact k-NN |
| **Lexical / keyword search, BM25** | Matching words, scored by term frequency | Not used (Neo4j full-text indexes provide it) | semantic search |
| **Hybrid search** | (a) vector + keyword, or (b) vector + graph | We do (b): vector entry points + graph hops | — |
| **Reranking** | Re-scoring retrieved items with another signal | similarity × importance × recency | retrieval |
| **RAG** | Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch, then put it in the prompt | `recall()` → memory block | fine-tuning |
| **GraphRAG** | RAG that uses a graph. Microsoft's GraphRAG builds community summaries over a whole corpus; "local" GraphRAG traverses from entry points | [Lesson 5](../lessons/05-vectors-and-graphrag.md) and the companion use the local style | — |

content.text:
The companion now runs on Qwen3-Embedding-8B. All 197 tests pass, and the scenarios passed 53 of 53 in both runs on Qwen. Nothing is committed yet.

**Turning it on and off**
- I added two lines to your `.env`: `EMBED_BASE_URL` (your DeepInfra URL) and `EMBED_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B`. It reuses `LLM_API_KEY`, so there's no new key.
- If you empty `EMBED_BASE_URL`, everything goes back to the local bge-small.
- Each model stores its vectors in its own property and indexes, so they don't overwrite each other and switching back costs nothing.
- The tests always run on the local model, offline.
- Lessons 5–7 still use the local model.

**Thresholds measured for Qwen**
Every cut-off had been tuned for bge-small, so I wrote [calibrate.py](companion/calibrate.py), which holds labelled yes/no pairs for each decision. What it found on Qwen:
- **Lower floors:** its scores for unrelated pairs are much lower than bge-small's. The old floors would have cut off most real matches, so the sensitive-memory and graph-hop floors went down.
- **The graph hop finally works:** at 0.85 it had never fired for indirect references on bge-small. With Qwen, "how is my kid doing?" now finds Logan.
- **Habits needed their own instruction:** without one, Qwen scored "heading to the gym" vs "went rock climbing" higher than two gym sentences, so the habit was never found.
- **"Loosely related" now comes from the vector score:** Qwen's score separates related from unrelated well enough to decide alone. The Lesson 18 cross-encoder had labelled "Mark's son Logan attends Elk Grove Elementary" as weak for "how is my kid doing?". In the web UI, "dogs" now shows `match 0.617 < 0.656`.

**Your data**
`python -m companion.reembed` gave your existing memories, people and episodes Qwen vectors (121 nodes in about 5 seconds). You'll need to rerun it after any future model change.

**Cost**
Recall now waits on one remote call per turn, about 0.3–0.6 s. Repeated texts are cached.

**New files**
- [companion/embeddings.py](companion/embeddings.py): local or remote embeddings, with one set of thresholds per model.
- [companion/reembed.py](companion/reembed.py): fills in vectors after a model switch.
- [lessons/19-choosing-an-embedding-model.md](lessons/19-choosing-an-embedding-model.md): the model comparison, the threshold table and what each number means. I also updated the README and glossary.
- [tests/test_19_embeddings.py](tests/test_19_embeddings.py): 11 tests.

**Not run:** the 42 LLM evals. They run on the local model, and that path didn't change apart from recall's relevance logic, which the regular tests cover.
